data_sources.name: WHO Global Health Estimates 2021
data_sources.brief: WHO's (World Health Organization) estimates of deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for every cause, country, age and sex. We used the 2021 country data for all ages and both sexes.

verification.summary: Every source below was checked on 29 September 2026. Scripts opened each link, compared titles with the official registries (Crossref, the DOI registry; PubMed Central, the US National Library of Medicine archive; WHO IRIS, the World Health Organization document library) and compared each burden figure with the live WHO data. Verification agents then read the source documents to confirm the figures and the cases.

source_primary.name: WHO Global Health Estimates 2021: disease burden (DALYs) by cause and country
source_primary.notes: Pulled from the WHO public API (https://xmart-api-public.who.int/DEX_CMS/GHE_FULL_DD), all ages, both sexes, the same data behind data.who.int country pages. Ranked items are WHO 'rankable' causes ordered by total DALYs. COVID-19 is excluded as a ranked item because 2021 is pandemic-distorted. Low-acuity, disability-only causes (back and neck pain, hearing loss, skin diseases, refractive errors, oral conditions, gynecological diseases, migraine, anxiety) are skipped so the list holds serious conditions; depression and self-harm are kept. Priority items come from WHO TB, malaria, HIV, hypertension and maternal mortality series (WHO GHO API and the WHO Global TB Programme estimates), IARC GLOBOCAN, PAHO, CDC and national surveys; each carries its own source_url. Known conflict: WHO GHE assigns dengue very few DALYs (rank 59 or lower in PHL, VNM, THA, DOM), while national surveillance shows very large case and hospital loads, so dengue is added as a priority item where surveillance supports it. Supplementary series use later years (TB 2024, malaria 2024, HIV 2025 (Philippines trend to 2024), maternal mortality 2023, hypertension 2019) than GHE 2021. IHME GBD 2021 was not used; its cause list and methods differ, so ranks can differ from these. Ranked items whose 'why' adds a TB, HIV or malaria figure draw it from https://www.who.int/teams/global-programme-on-tuberculosis-and-lung-health/data, https://www.who.int/data/gho/data/themes/hiv-aids and https://www.who.int/data/gho/data/indicators/indicator-details/GHO/estimated-number-of-malaria-cases.

sources.name: MedEdPORTAL
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 or CC BY (per publication)
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed, PubMed-indexed open-access journal of teaching materials. Each publication ships the facilitator guide, SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) case and checklists.
sources.brief: The largest free, peer-reviewed library of standardized patient cases, OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination: a timed exam station where a student sees a standardized patient) stations and simulation scenarios. Written mostly for US programs.

sources.name: EM Sim Cases
sources.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed FOAM case bank run by Canadian EM simulation faculty (McMaster, McGill, Queen's, UBC and others). Each case has a vignette, learning objectives, case progression, and debrief notes. Site footer states CC BY-SA 4.0.
sources.brief: Free Canadian bank of about 150 emergency simulation cases. Written for mannequin-based team training, with enough history detail to adapt for a standardized patient.

sources.name: Cureus simulation technical reports
sources.publisher: Cureus Journal of Medical Science (Springer Nature)
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 (older articles CC BY 3.0)
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed open-access journal with a Medical Simulation section and technical report format for full scenarios. cureus.com blocks automated requests (HTTP 403), so case links point to the identical full text on PubMed Central, which resolves.
sources.brief: Open journal that publishes complete simulation scenarios as technical reports, including some written for Kenya, Malawi and India. Each report has the case script, critical actions and a debrief guide.

sources.name: EM ReSCu Peds (Emergency Medicine Resident Simulation Curriculum for Pediatrics)
sources.publisher: ALiEM (Academic Life in Emergency Medicine) with 10 national EM and pediatric organizations
sources.license: Free access; ALiEM content is marked All Rights Reserved
sources.trust_note: 16 peer-reviewed cases built by more than 50 pediatric simulation experts from 44 institutions; each case names its authors and editors. Implementation is described in Cureus (2026).
sources.brief: A free national pediatric simulation curriculum of 16 cases for emergency residents. Each case has setup, history, vital sign progression, critical actions and a debrief guide.

sources.name: ACEP SimBox (Pediatric Readiness SimBox)
sources.publisher: SimBox Creative Team with the American College of Emergency Physicians and the EMSC Innovation and Improvement Center
sources.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (stated on newer case booklets; others not stated)
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed, low-technology pediatric simulation program for community emergency departments, described in Annals of Emergency Medicine (2021) and Cureus. Case booklets plus video vital-sign monitors; used in many countries.
sources.brief: Free downloadable pediatric emergency drills that need only a doll or low-cost mannequin and a screen. Good fit for low-resource sites because no high-fidelity equipment is needed.

sources.name: SIM Scenario Exchange
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (per scenario pages checked)
sources.trust_note: National Canadian simulation network; scenarios are contributed by colleges, universities and hospitals and some are peer reviewed. A free account is needed to download. The site blocks automated requests (HTTP 403); pages were confirmed with a fetch tool.
sources.brief: Open exchange of nursing, paramedic and medical simulation scenarios, many as virtual patients. Strong on nursing mental health and paramedic cases.

sources.name: CDC Self-Study Modules on Tuberculosis
sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Division of Tuberculosis Elimination
sources.license: Public domain (US government work)
sources.trust_note: Official CDC (US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) training series (Modules 1 to 9, updated page March 2025). Each module has short case studies with answer keys.
sources.brief: Nine free PDF modules on TB (tuberculosis) transmission, diagnosis, treatment, adherence and contact investigation. The short case studies suit communication role-plays on adherence and treatment.

sources.name: Curry International Tuberculosis Center products
sources.publisher: University of California San Francisco, Curry International Tuberculosis Center
sources.license: Free access; copyright Regents of the University of California
sources.trust_note: CDC-funded TB (tuberculosis) Center of Excellence. Materials are expert reviewed; most are guides and toolkits rather than full patient cases.
sources.brief: Free TB (tuberculosis) guides, toolkits and self-study tools, including radiology practice cases and the Drug-Resistant TB Survival Guide. Good background for building TB and MDR-TB (multidrug-resistant tuberculosis) scenarios.

sources.name: Global Tuberculosis Institute educational materials
sources.publisher: Rutgers New Jersey Medical School, Global Tuberculosis Institute
sources.license: Free access; copyright Rutgers University, all rights reserved
sources.trust_note: CDC-funded TB (tuberculosis) Center of Excellence. No public patient case bank found; the TB Interview manual and interview checklist support interview skills training.
sources.brief: Free TB (tuberculosis) training products, including a TB interview manual with feedback forms and a contact investigation interview checklist. Useful to design and score an SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) interview station.

sources.name: National HIV Curriculum (Case Discussions podcast)
sources.publisher: University of Washington, funded by HRSA
sources.license: Free access; copyright University of Washington (optional free registration for CE)
sources.trust_note: Nationally used US HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) curriculum. Case discussion episodes walk through a single patient with an infectious disease expert, with full transcripts.
sources.brief: Free HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) lessons plus podcast episodes that follow one patient from presentation to management. Cases cover cryptococcal meningitis, toxoplasmosis, PCP and other opportunistic infections.

sources.name: Hepatitis B Online
sources.license: Free access; copyright University of Washington
sources.trust_note: Authoritative free curriculum. No patient case collection was found on the site; content is lesson based.
sources.brief: Free lessons on hepatitis B testing, treatment and liver cancer screening. Use it as the reference behind an HBV (hepatitis B virus) or HCC (hepatocellular carcinoma, the main liver cancer) SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) case, not as a case source.

sources.name: Hepatitis C Online (Expert Opinions cases)
sources.license: Free access; copyright University of Washington
sources.trust_note: Short clinical vignettes with answers from named hepatitis experts. Vignettes are brief, so an educator must add history and exam detail.
sources.brief: Free short cases on hepatitis C and cirrhosis decisions, each with expert commentary. Good seeds for an outpatient counseling station.

sources.name: Gorgas Course Case of the Week
sources.publisher: University of Alabama at Birmingham and Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia
sources.license: Free access; no open licence stated (copyright UAB)
sources.trust_note: Real inpatient cases from the Tropical Disease Unit, Cayetano Heredia Hospital, Lima, Peru, run since 2009. Each case gives history, exposure, exam, images, diagnosis and discussion.
sources.brief: Weekly real tropical medicine cases from Peru with a full history, exposure history, exam and images. The structured history makes them very easy to turn into SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) scripts.

sources.name: American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene (case reports and Images in Clinical Tropical Medicine)
sources.publisher: American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
sources.license: Free to read; older articles copyright ASTMH, many recent articles CC BY or CC BY-NC
sources.trust_note: Leading peer-reviewed tropical medicine journal. Image items are short, so history detail is limited.
sources.brief: Peer-reviewed tropical case reports and one-image teaching cases. Strong on field settings in Asia, Africa and Latin America.

sources.name: PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases (case reports and photo quizzes)
sources.license: CC BY
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed open access journal. Case items and photo quizzes are few but well documented.
sources.brief: Open access journal with occasional photo quizzes and case reports on neglected tropical diseases. All content is CC BY.

sources.name: Malaria Journal
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 (some recent articles CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed open access journal dedicated to malaria. Case reports include full clinical course.
sources.brief: Open access malaria journal with detailed case reports on severe, cerebral, congenital and drug-resistant malaria.

sources.name: Journal of Medical Case Reports
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 (some recent articles CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed case report journal. Uses a structured format (patient information, findings, timeline, outcome) that maps well to SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) scripts.
sources.brief: Large open access case report journal with many cases from South Asia and Africa. The structured layout gives history, exam, tests and outcome in order.

sources.name: Pan African Medical Journal
sources.license: CC BY (Creative Commons Attribution License)
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed African open access journal. Many case reports are in French; 'Images in medicine' items are short.
sources.brief: Open access African journal with case reports and image cases from African and Indian hospitals. Good source of locally set cases.

sources.name: IDCases
sources.license: CC BY or CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (author choice; most cases here are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed open access infectious disease case journal (ISSN 2214-2509). Many cases are from high-income settings, so filter by country. The publisher site blocks automated link checks; the URL was confirmed by search.
sources.brief: Open access infectious disease case reports. Useful for typhoid, TB-HIV (tuberculosis with HIV infection) and envenoming complications.

sources.name: Clinical Case Reports
sources.license: CC BY, CC BY-NC or CC BY-NC-ND (varies by article)
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed, fully open access case journal (ISSN 2050-0904) with many authors from Nepal, Uganda, Cameroon and Tanzania. The publisher site blocks automated link checks; the URL was confirmed by search.
sources.brief: Open access case reports, often from LMIC (low- and middle-income countries) hospitals. Each has a short key clinical message that can become a learning objective.

sources.name: BMC Infectious Diseases (case reports)
sources.license: CC BY 4.0
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed open access journal. Case reports include detailed lab and CSF (cerebrospinal fluid) data.
sources.brief: Open access infectious disease journal with detailed case reports, including HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis cases from Malawi, Uganda and India.

sources.name: PubMed Central (other open access case reports)
sources.license: Varies by article (listed per case)
sources.trust_note: Free full-text archive of peer-reviewed articles. Used here for single cases from journals outside the named list.
sources.brief: Free archive of full-text articles. Search with the filter 'case reports' plus a country name to find locally set cases.

sources.name: Open-i biomedical image search
sources.license: Varies by source article (images from open access PMC articles)
sources.trust_note: NLM search engine over figures from open access articles. Good for finding a real rash, X-ray or smear image to add to a case.
sources.brief: Free search of images from open access articles. Use it to add real clinical images (smears, X-rays, skin signs) to an SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) case, citing the source article.

sources.name: Journal of Education and Teaching in Emergency Medicine (JETem)
sources.publisher: JETem, in partnership with the Western Journal of Emergency Medicine (University of California eScholarship)
sources.license: CC BY 4.0
sources.trust_note: Peer reviewed, open access, indexed in PubMed Central. The site footer licenses content under CC BY 4.0. Each article has a free manuscript PDF with case script, vitals, labs, critical actions and debrief notes.
sources.brief: Free peer reviewed emergency medicine simulation cases and oral board style cases with full facilitator scripts. Most are written for high fidelity mannequins in US emergency departments, but many adapt well to a standardized patient or a low resource setting.

sources.name: SAEM Simulation Academy case documents
sources.license: unknown
sources.trust_note: Scenario templates hosted on the SAEM (Society for Academic Emergency Medicine) website by its simulation interest group. Free PDFs, not peer reviewed as a set, with no license stated and no public index page (found by direct document links).
sources.brief: A small set of free emergency medicine scenario PDFs with objectives, critical actions and scripts. Useful as extra cases, but authorship, dates and reuse terms are unclear.

sources.name: Advancing Care Excellence (ACE) unfolding cases: ACE.S, ACE.V, ACE.Z, ACE.D
sources.license: Free to download for teaching; copyright National League for Nursing (no open license stated)
sources.trust_note: Written by nurse educators and reviewed by the NLN (most cases reviewed 2023 to 2024). Each case has a first-person patient monologue (audio and script), three simulation scenarios, chart materials and an instructor toolkit, so SPs (standardized patients: trained actors who play a patient) can use them directly.
sources.brief: Free unfolding cases about older adults, veterans, people with dementia and people with disabilities. Each case follows one patient and family across three encounters, with scripts ready for an actor.

sources.name: CAN-Sim open-access virtual simulation games
sources.publisher: Canadian Alliance of Nurse Educators using Simulation (CAN-Sim)
sources.license: Free open access for listed games; no license stated on game pages. Some games linked from the list (for example diabetic ketoacidosis) are for members only.
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed virtual gaming simulations built by Canadian university nursing programs (Thompson Rivers, Nipissing, Queen's, Ottawa) with CAN-Sim. Branching video games; the patient story can be adapted into an SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) script.
sources.brief: Free, branching video simulations for nursing students. Learners make choices at each step and see the result, then debrief.

sources.name: ARISE simulation scenarios (Wisconsin Technical College System)
sources.publisher: Wisconsin Technical College System consortium via SkillsCommons (MERLOT)
sources.license: Creative Commons (US Department of Labor TAACCCT grant materials); check the license on each item
sources.trust_note: 150 low- and high-fidelity nursing and allied health scenarios aligned with the WTCS statewide nursing curriculum. The ARIS app they used is no longer supported, and in September 2026 individual SkillsCommons item links (for example the ARISE heart failure scenarios) returned 404, so reach items through the showcase page.
sources.brief: A large set of free nursing simulation scenarios from Wisconsin technical colleges, each with a patient storyline and a live simulated patient introduction.

sources.name: Open RN virtual simulations
sources.publisher: Open RN project, Chippewa Valley Technical College (WTCS), funded by the US Department of Education
sources.license: CC BY 4.0
sources.trust_note: Faculty-built against the WTCS nursing curriculum and the NCLEX-RN test plan. Free H5P virtual simulations with patient and family videos; no login needed.
sources.brief: Free online branching simulations for nursing students, all CC BY 4.0. Patient videos and case details can be reused to write SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) scripts.

sources.name: Laerdal Scenario Cloud (formerly SimStore and complimentary scenarios)
sources.license: Proprietary; subscription (free trial available)
sources.trust_note: Manufacturer scenarios written for Laerdal manikins. The old complimentary scenarios page now redirects to the subscription Scenario Cloud.
sources.brief: Laerdal's scenario library for its manikins. It needs a paid subscription, so no cases are listed here.

sources.name: Free NAC examination resources (sample OSCE case studies)
sources.license: Free to use for exam preparation; copyright Medical Council of Canada
sources.trust_note: Official national licensing body. Each sample case has candidate instructions, the full SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) role (history, timeline, affect) and the scoring approach. The page blocks automated checks; the PDFs resolve directly.
sources.brief: Official sample OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination: a timed exam station where a student sees a standardized patient) stations from Canada's national exam for international medical graduates. Each PDF gives the full patient script and what examiners look for.

sources.name: USMLE Step 2 Clinical Skills (legacy)
sources.license: Copyright USMLE
sources.trust_note: Step 2 CS was discontinued in January 2021. The official site no longer offers the sample case or patient note materials, so there is nothing to reuse from the official source.
sources.brief: The US standardized patient exam that ended in 2021. Its old sample case is no longer on the official site.

sources.name: Association of Standardized Patient Educators (ASPE)
sources.license: Varies; some resources are for members only
sources.trust_note: The international professional body for SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) educators. It publishes the ASPE (Association of Standardized Patient Educators) Standards of Best Practice and a free case development template, which are useful for writing and checking SP scripts. It does not offer a public case bank.
sources.brief: Standards and templates for building SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) programs and writing SP cases. Use it to check the quality of any script in this library.

sources.name: Advances in Simulation
sources.license: CC BY 4.0
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed open-access simulation journal. Good for SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) methods (it published the ASPE (Association of Standardized Patient Educators) Standards of Best Practice in 2017); full SP scripts are rare.
sources.brief: Open-access research journal on healthcare simulation. Useful for SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) methods and debriefing, less so for ready-made cases.

sources.name: International Journal of Healthcare Simulation (IJoHS)
sources.license: Open access; check the license on each article (APCs since April 2024)
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed open-access journal, official journal of the Association for Simulated Practice in Healthcare (ASPiH) and of simulation societies in India and Pan Asia. Its archive is at archive.johs.org.uk and new articles go to the Journal of Healthcare Simulation. The old domain ijohs.com now shows unrelated commercial content, so do not link to it.
sources.brief: Open-access simulation journal with strong UK, India and Asia links. Search it for scenario and technical reports.

sources.name: MedEdPublish
sources.publisher: AMEE (Association for Medical Education in Europe), F1000 platform
sources.license: CC BY 4.0
sources.trust_note: Open-access, open peer review. Articles are published before review, so check the review status of each item.
sources.brief: Open-access health professions education journal. It has some SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) and simulation descriptions but few full scripts.

sources.name: OpenLabyrinth virtual patient platform
sources.publisher: OpenLabyrinth consortium (University of Calgary and partners)
sources.license: Software GPL-3.0; case licenses vary by author
sources.trust_note: Open-source branching virtual patient platform used by eViP partners. The demo server hosts open cases; the main openlabyrinth.ca site returned a server error in September 2026. Source code is at github.com/olab/Open-Labyrinth.
sources.brief: Free software for building and playing branching virtual patients. Local teams can host it and write their own cases.

sources.name: eViP Electronic Virtual Patients referatory
sources.publisher: eViP consortium (EU eContentplus project, led by St George's, University of London)
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0
sources.trust_note: Listing of 340 repurposed virtual patients from European medical schools. The project has ended and the site is not updated; some player links (for example old OpenLabyrinth links at St George's) no longer work, so test each case before use.
sources.brief: A free catalog of virtual patients in several languages, all CC BY-NC-SA. Some cases still open in their original players.

sources.name: Aquifer virtual patient cases
sources.license: Proprietary; institutional or individual subscription
sources.trust_note: Widely used in US medical schools, peer-reviewed cases, but paid. No cases are listed here.
sources.brief: High-quality US virtual patient cases that need a paid subscription.

sources.name: OPENPediatrics
sources.license: Free for health professionals after registration; terms of use apply (no open license stated)
sources.trust_note: Pediatric critical care and clinical education videos and interactive modules for clinicians worldwide. Not SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) scripts.
sources.brief: Free pediatric teaching videos and modules after sign-up. Useful background for pediatric simulations, not a case bank.

sources.name: mhGAP training manuals (mhGAP-IG version 2.0)
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
sources.trust_note: WHO (World Health Organization) training package for non-specialist health workers in low-resource settings (WHO/MSD/MER/17.6, 2017). Each module has scripted role plays with separate instructions for the health worker, the person seeking help and the observer.
sources.brief: WHO (World Health Organization) role-play scripts for depression, suicide risk, alcohol use and dementia, written for primary care in low-resource countries. They work as SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) scripts with little change.

sources.name: EQUIP (Ensuring Quality in Psychological Support)
sources.license: No license stated on the resources page
sources.trust_note: WHO (World Health Organization) and UNICEF (United Nations Children's Fund) platform for competency-based training of mental health and psychosocial support helpers, used in 36 countries by 2024. It gives example standardized role-play scripts (English and Spanish) for its ENACT and other competency tools.
sources.brief: Free WHO (World Health Organization) and UNICEF (United Nations Children's Fund) role-play scripts to test basic counseling skills. Registration is needed for the full platform.

sources.name: BMC open-access journals (BMC Medical Education, Trials)
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 for most articles; check each article
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed open-access journals. SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) scripts, when shared, are usually in the additional files.
sources.brief: Open-access journals where some studies publish their SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) cases and OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination: a timed exam station where a student sees a standardized patient) stations as supplements.

sources.name: PLOS Medicine and PLOS Global Public Health
sources.license: CC BY 4.0
sources.trust_note: Peer-reviewed open-access journals. Standardized patient research studies in LMICs (low- and middle-income countries) publish their case scenarios and SP training methods here.
sources.brief: Open-access journals with standardized patient studies from India, Kenya and other LMICs (low- and middle-income countries), including their case scenarios.

sources.name: Basic Emergency Care: approach to the acutely ill and injured (participant workbook)
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
sources.trust_note: WHO/ICRC course for first-contact emergency providers in low-resource settings; each module ends with two facilitator-led case scenarios (adult and child) that participants must lead to pass.
sources.brief: Five modules (ABCDE (Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure), trauma, difficulty in breathing, shock, altered mental status) with ten scripted adult and child case scenarios plus handover (SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation: a handover format)) examples.

sources.name: Emergency Triage Assessment and Treatment (ETAT): manual for participants and facilitator guide
sources.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
sources.trust_note: WHO (World Health Organization) paediatric triage course (2005). The facilitator guide, module six, has 14 scripted case management scenarios with facilitator inputs and expected responses.
sources.brief: Paediatric emergency triage course. The facilitator guide scripts 14 child emergencies (shock, dehydration, convulsion, respiratory distress, trauma) for role play.

sources.name: ETAT+ course (Kenya Paediatric Association / KEMRI-Wellcome)
sources.publisher: Kenya Paediatric Association (KPA) and KEPRECON, with KEMRI-Wellcome Trust
sources.license: Not stated on the course page; free PDF modules posted by KPA
sources.trust_note: Kenyan adaptation of WHO (World Health Organization) ETAT (Emergency Triage Assessment and Treatment) with neonatal care and national guideline content; more than 10,000 health workers trained since 2006. Individual scenarios were not verified for this catalog.
sources.brief: Free downloadable ETAT (Emergency Triage Assessment and Treatment)+ modules (triage, newborn resuscitation, respiratory distress, dehydration). The course itself is taught in person by KPA instructors.

sources.name: Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI): distance learning course
sources.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
sources.trust_note: Official WHO (World Health Organization) IMCI (Integrated Management of Childhood Illness) self-study course (2014, 9 modules). Each module opens with a named child case study that runs through the module, plus DVD video cases.
sources.brief: Nine self-study modules for first-level health workers, each built around a story of a sick child and caregiver that can be turned into a caregiver role play.

sources.name: mhGAP training manuals for the mhGAP Intervention Guide version 2.0 (ToT and ToHP)
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
sources.trust_note: WHO (World Health Organization) mental health training package (2017, field-test version). Supporting material for each module has role plays with separate scripts for the person seeking help, the health-care provider and the observer, plus competency forms.
sources.brief: Ready-made three-role scripts (patient, provider, observer) for depression, psychosis, epilepsy, child mental health, dementia, substance use, self-harm and suicide, and other complaints.

sources.name: Training course on the inpatient management of severe acute malnutrition (2021 update)
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
sources.trust_note: WHO (World Health Organization) course with eight modules plus facilitator and clinical instructor guides. Module 3 (initial management) uses named child cases for written exercises on the Critical Care Pathway form.
sources.brief: Case exercises on children with severe wasting who also have dehydration, shock, hypothermia or low blood sugar, using the WHO (World Health Organization) Critical Care Pathway form.

sources.name: Handbook for clinical management of dengue
sources.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
sources.trust_note: WHO (World Health Organization) handbook (2012) whose Section 4 has four detailed, time-stamped real-world case studies with commentary on pitfalls. WHO WPRO (WHO Western Pacific Regional Office) also publishes a Dengue clinical management facilitator's training manual (2013, iris.who.int/handle/10665/207673) with case studies and role plays, but its case handouts are not printed in the manual.
sources.brief: Four teaching cases of severe dengue in adults and children, showing missed shock, hidden bleeding and fluid overload, with expert discussion.

sources.name: Clinical diagnosis and management of dengue (self-learning course)
sources.publisher: PAHO Virtual Campus for Public Health
sources.license: PAHO terms; free, open to the public
sources.trust_note: Free PAHO/WHO self-paced course in English, Spanish and Portuguese for doctors, nurses and students; covers warning signs, severity classification and treatment.
sources.brief: Free online dengue course from PAHO (Pan American Health Organization). Useful background before running dengue SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) cases; individual cases not verified for this catalog.

sources.name: CDC dengue clinical management courses (including Virtual Practice in Dengue Management Through Simulated Scenarios, WB4964)
sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.license: US government course; free with CE credit via CDC TRAIN
sources.trust_note: Three free CDC (US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) TRAIN courses: an integrated approach module (WB4945), a case-based module Face the Case (WB4963) and a simulated-scenario module (WB4964).
sources.brief: Free CDC (US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) online courses with case-based and simulated dengue patients; registration on CDC TRAIN needed. The CDC site blocks automated checks, so the page was confirmed through a browser fetch.

sources.name: WHO Essential Newborn Care course (ENC 1 and ENC 2), including simulation practice cards
sources.publisher: WHO (with Helping Mothers and Babies Survive)
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
sources.trust_note: WHO (World Health Organization) 2024 revision of essential newborn care training in the Helping Babies Survive style. Simulation practice cards give scripted cases for two or three people, with mother prompts and a debrief.
sources.brief: Free action plans, flip charts, provider guides and simulation practice cards for newborn resuscitation, routine care and care of small and sick babies.

sources.name: Helping Babies Survive: Helping Babies Breathe (HBB 2nd ed.), Essential Care for Every Baby (ECEB), Essential Care for Small Babies (ECSB)
sources.publisher: American Academy of Pediatrics (with Laerdal Global Health)
sources.license: Copyright American Academy of Pediatrics, all rights reserved; free download for training use
sources.trust_note: AAP (American Academy of Pediatrics) programs taught to more than 850,000 providers in 80+ countries. OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination: a timed exam station where a student sees a standardized patient) sheets give a role-play case the facilitator reads aloud, with prompts and a done/not done checklist.
sources.brief: Free OSCEs (Objective Structured Clinical Examinations: timed exam stations where a student sees a standardized patient), knowledge checks and skill checks for newborn resuscitation and essential newborn care. AAP (American Academy of Pediatrics) states the HBB (Helping Babies Breathe) action plan, flip chart and provider guide can be downloaded at no cost from its International Resources site; printed copies are sold.

sources.name: Helping Mothers Survive (Pre-eclampsia and Eclampsia, Bleeding After Birth and other modules)
sources.license: Copyright Jhpiego, all rights reserved; free download from Jhpiego
sources.trust_note: Jhpiego low-dose, high-frequency simulation program used in 65+ countries. Facilitator flip charts contain scripted simulation cases with only-if-assessed findings and structured debriefs.
sources.brief: Free action plans and facilitator flip charts for obstetric emergency drills. The Pre-eclampsia and Eclampsia flip chart (June 2026 edition) has role-play cases for severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia.

sources.name: Bleeding after birth: course on prevention, diagnosis and treatment of postpartum haemorrhage
sources.publisher: WHO (developed with Jhpiego from the HMS Bleeding After Birth module)
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
sources.trust_note: WHO (World Health Organization) 2025 course aligned with the new PPH (postpartum hemorrhage) diagnostic criteria and the PPH bundle. The flip chart has five scenario practices with simulator settings, prompts and expected actions; six OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination: a timed exam station where a student sees a standardized patient) cases are on www.who.int/tools/bleeding-after-birth.
sources.brief: One-day simulation course for all birth attendants on preventing, spotting early and treating bleeding after birth, with scripted scenarios and OSCEs (Objective Structured Clinical Examinations: timed exam stations where a student sees a standardized patient).

sources.name: Package of Essential Noncommunicable (PEN) disease and healthy lifestyle interventions: training modules for primary health care workers
sources.publisher: WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
sources.trust_note: WHO (World Health Organization) SEARO training modules (2018) for primary care workers; activities include short case studies, case scenarios and two-person role plays with answers for the facilitator.
sources.brief: NCD (noncommunicable disease) training for primary care with short cases on diabetes emergencies, blood pressure, stroke, COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) and asthma, oral cancer, plus role plays for RHD (rheumatic heart disease), breast findings, tobacco and alcohol brief advice.

sources.name: IMAI TB-HIV co-management training course: participant's manual
sources.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
sources.trust_note: WHO (World Health Organization) IMAI (Integrated Management of Adolescent and Adult Illness) course (2008) for first-level facility workers. It uses expert patient trainers (EPTs), people living with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) who play the patient and give one-to-one feedback, plus written case studies.
sources.brief: Case studies and expert-patient role plays for finding TB (tuberculosis) in people with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus), starting treatment and preparing patients for ART (antiretroviral therapy).

sources.name: Primary Trauma Care course manual (2018 edition)
sources.license: Copyright 2018 Primary Trauma Care Foundation; may be copied for courses with permission from PTCF
sources.trust_note: Manual originated as an annex to WHO (World Health Organization) Surgical Care at the District Hospital (2003); taught in 76 countries. The 2018 manual text has no written case scenarios; scenarios are run by course instructors.
sources.brief: Free trauma manual (ABCDE (Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure) primary survey, secondary survey, triage) useful as the reference for trauma SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) cases.

sources.name: Safe Delivery App
sources.publisher: Maternity Foundation (with Universities of Copenhagen and Southern Denmark)
sources.license: Free app (iOS and Android, offline); Maternity Foundation terms
sources.trust_note: Widely used offline job aid and training app for skilled birth attendants with animated videos, action cards and a certification track (MyLearning).
sources.brief: Free midwifery app with animated instruction for emergency obstetric and newborn care. Specific in-app cases were not verified for this catalog.

sources.name: Global Health Media Project videos
sources.license: Free; download requires accepting GHMP Terms for Video Download Use
sources.trust_note: More than 300 live-action teaching videos on newborn care, childbirth, small babies, nutrition and emergency care, in 119 languages.
sources.brief: Short real-patient videos that show signs and skills; good for SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) trainer calibration, not scripted cases.

sources.name: AFEM resources (curriculum, Rapid Assessment Protocols, presentation bank)
sources.license: Described by AFEM as almost entirely open source; per-item terms not stated
sources.trust_note: Africa-specific emergency care curriculum and teaching materials from the continental emergency medicine federation. Case scenarios were not verified in these files.
sources.brief: Free African emergency medicine curricula and slide banks to anchor local SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) emergency cases.

sources.name: HEARTS technical package for cardiovascular disease management in primary health care
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
sources.trust_note: WHO (World Health Organization) technical package (2016, risk-based module 2020) with protocols, counselling and team-care modules; no scripted patient cases were found.
sources.brief: Reference protocols for building hypertension and CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) cases; not a case collection.

sources.name: IARC screening atlases and e-learning (Atlas of Colposcopy, Atlas of VIA, Atlas of oral cancer and precancer)
sources.publisher: International Agency for Research on Cancer (WHO)
sources.license: Copyright IARC; free access under IARC terms of use
sources.trust_note: WHO (World Health Organization) cancer agency image atlases, organized as illustrated clinical cases by diagnosis (normal, inflammation, low and high grade lesions, cancer, post-treatment) with quizzes.
sources.brief: Image-based cases for cervical and oral screening; pair images with an SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) history for a screening OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination: a timed exam station where a student sees a standardized patient) station.

sources.name: RHDAustralia free online learning programs
sources.publisher: RHDAustralia (Menzies School of Health Research) and Heart Foundation
sources.license: Free, accredited; Heart Foundation learning hub terms
sources.trust_note: National Australian ARF and RHD (rheumatic heart disease) program; guideline authors. Eight free self-paced programs including a patient-story module (Michael's Story).
sources.brief: Free accredited e-learning on recognizing acute rheumatic fever, penicillin prophylaxis and RHD (rheumatic heart disease) in pregnancy.

cases.title: Unresponsive Patient in the Post Anesthesia Care Unit
diagnoses: Unresponsive patient after anesthesia (four possible causes)
presentations: unresponsive in the postanesthesia care unit
cases.brief: A patient is unresponsive in the postanesthesia recovery unit, with the same front story but four possible causes across four scenarios. Learners explore diagnoses and practice care across the perioperative period.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Stroke Code Simulation for Medical Education
cases.learners: neurology and emergency residents, medical students, nurses
cases.brief: A patient with acute stroke symptoms is portrayed by a standardized patient. Learners run a stroke code, use the NIH Stroke Scale, and make time-critical treatment decisions as team leaders.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Calcium Channel Blocker Overdose Simulation
cases.learners: emergency, internal medicine and family medicine residents
cases.brief: A patient arrives after an unknown ingestion that proves to be a cardiotoxic calcium channel blocker. Learners practice exam, clinical reasoning, and treatment of the poisoning and its complications.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Pediatric Emergency Medicine Simulation Curriculum: Bronchiolitis
cases.brief: A critically ill infant with bronchiolitis presents to the emergency department. Learners practice recognizing severe illness and managing it with high flow nasal cannula oxygen and other support, using a manikin.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Pediatric Emergency Medicine Simulation Curriculum: Blunt Abdominal Trauma
cases.brief: A child arrives with blunt abdominal trauma at risk of shock or bowel injury. Learners practice rapid assessment, resuscitation, airway decisions, and arranging definitive care.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: A Breaking Bad News Exercise to Assess Student Competence Prior to Graduation
presentations: family meeting about change in patient condition
cases.brief: An SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) plays an upset family member of a hospitalized patient across several meetings as the patient's condition changes. Students practice breaking bad news and are assessed on milestones.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Obstructive Mucus Plug in the Prone Position
diagnoses: Airway obstruction from mucus plug in prone position
presentations: loss of end tidal CO2 and ventilation during spine surgery
cases.brief: A 42-year-old male smoker having spinal surgery in the prone position suddenly has complete airway obstruction. Learners practice diagnosis, management, and crisis resource management.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: A Large Scale Interprofessional Simulation Experience for Medical, Nursing, and Pharmacy Students
diagnoses: Critical medical condition requiring transfer to acute care
presentations: deterioration needing hand-off from clinic to hospital
cases.brief: An SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) with a common critical medical condition moves from an ambulatory setting to acute care. Interprofessional student teams practice triage, recognizing the need for transfer, and hand-off communication.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Altered Mental Status in a Toddler
presentations: altered mental status in a toddler
cases.brief: A 2-year-old has altered mental status from cerebral sinovenous thrombosis after iron deficiency anemia and dehydration. Actors follow scripts while learners examine the child and work through a rare diagnosis.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Breast Cancer Instructional Module
diagnoses: Early and late stage breast cancer
presentations: breast cancer prevention, diagnosis and treatment
cases.brief: Small groups discuss short answer patient cases on breast cancer. Learners practice decisions on prevention, diagnosis and treatment across early and late disease.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Aligning Institutional OSCEs with Clinical Learning Environment Review Focus Areas and Competencies
cases.brief: Five OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination: a timed exam station where a student sees a standardized patient) stations cover delivering bad news, error disclosure, informed consent, and surgical and medical health care disparities. Residents are scored on communication by trained SPs (standardized patients: trained actors who play a patient).
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Scott Green: Depression after a Heart Attack
cases.brief: Scott Green is a patient who had a heart attack and is now depressed. Students take a chronic disease history and practice recognizing and treating depression.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Spiritual Histories: Putting Religio-Cultural Competence into Practice
diagnoses: Spiritual and religious influences on care
cases.brief: Two case studies and two role plays let students practice taking a spiritual history. They learn how to ask about religious beliefs and practices and use the answers in care.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Interprofessional Team-Based Learning Module: Dementia, Depression, and Delirium
presentations: cognitive and mood changes in an older adult
cases.learners: internal medicine residents, pharmacy residents, psychology students
cases.brief: Interprofessional teams work through a geriatric patient case with dementia, depression and delirium. They practice prioritizing evaluation and treatment among competing diagnoses.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Introduction to Pediatrics: A Patient with Difficult Intravenous Access
presentations: need for IV access in a child
cases.brief: A child with difficult intravenous access needs an IV placed. Learners practice handling the situation in a repeatable, observable simulation.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Neonatal Ethics Teaching Program – Scenario-Oriented Learning in Ethics: Antenatal Consultation at the Limit of Viability
diagnoses: Threatened preterm birth at the limit of viability
cases.brief: An SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) plays a parent in an antenatal consultation at the limit of viability. Trainees practice communication and apply ethical principles when discussing options.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Simulation of Urgent Airway Management in a Postthyroidectomy Hematoma
cases.brief: A 68-year-old man has an expanding neck hematoma 2 hours after total thyroidectomy. Residents gather history and exam findings, secure the airway, and decide on bedside evacuation before definitive surgery.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Learning to Beat the Shock Clock: A Low-Fidelity Simulation Board Game for Pediatric and Emergency Medicine Residents
diagnoses: Pediatric septic shock from urinary tract infection
cases.brief: In a tabletop board game, residents manage a healthy 12-year-old boy in cold shock from a urinary tract infection and a 5-year-old girl with leukemia in warm shock from pneumonia. They practice recognizing and treating septic shock.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Using Motivational Interviewing to Address Tobacco Cessation: Two Standardized Patient Cases for Pediatric Residents
diagnoses: Tobacco use and exposure in parents of pediatric patients

cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Inappropriately Firing Defibrillator: A Simulation Case for Emergency Medicine Residents
cases.brief: A 63-year-old man arrives after feeling his implanted defibrillator fire and is found to have supraventricular tachycardia with an inappropriately firing device. Residents recognize the problem and manage it.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Acute Neuromuscular Respiratory Weakness Due to Acute Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy (AIDP): A Simulation Scenario for Neurology Providers
cases.brief: A live standardized patient has respiratory weakness from Guillain-Barre syndrome. Learners assess the patient, recognize impending respiratory failure, and start early ventilatory support, with a checklist and debriefing guide provided.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: ICU Emergencies Simulation Curriculum for Critical Care Fellows: Neurologic Emergencies
cases.brief: Three ICU (intensive care unit) neurologic emergencies are provided: symptomatic hyponatremia, severe alcohol withdrawal, and brain herniation. Each has objectives, critical action checklists, and debriefing material.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Geriatrics 5Ms for Primary Care Workshop

cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Delivering Challenging News: An Illness-Trajectory Communication Curriculum for Multispecialty Oncology Residents and Fellows
diagnoses: Cancer diagnosis, relapse, and poor prognosis disclosure

cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: A Simulated Mass Casualty Incident Triage Exercise: SimWars
diagnoses: Mass casualty incident from gas line explosion and building collapse

cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.brief: A two-station OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination: a timed exam station where a student sees a standardized patient) has residents interview Spanish-speaking standardized patients through a professional interpreter. cases.brief: A 55-year-old man has symptoms of acute stroke and a solo resident must rate stroke severity, coordinate hospital resources, and discuss thrombolysis risks and benefits. The resident then handles complications and raised intracranial pressure.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.brief: A 5-year-old boy with asthma has had 2 days of upper respiratory symptoms and now presents in status asthmaticus. Residents are assessed with a validated checklist on recognizing and treating the exacerbation.

cases.title: Discharge Day: A Case-Based Interprofessional Exercise About Team Collaboration in Pediatrics
cases.learners: pediatrics rotation medical students, social work, nursing, pharmacy, nutrition trainees

cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.learners: OB-GYN (obstetrics and gynecology) residents (PGY (postgraduate year) 1-4), nurses
cases.brief: A simulated pregnant patient with blood pressure and fetal monitoring needs a history and exam, then diagnosis and treatment of pre-eclampsia, severe-range blood pressures, and eclampsia. Performance is scored on a checklist with a debriefing.
cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Clinical Reasoning in the Ward Setting: A Rapid Response Scenario for Residents and Attendings
presentations: rapid response call with rising acuity

cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Common Variable Immunodeficiency: A Standardized Patient Case for Second-Year Medical Students

cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Pediatric Acute Care Simulator Case: Apnea
cases.brief: A 6-year-old is brought to the emergency department by ambulance after being found unresponsive at his grandmother's house. Residents are assessed with a validated checklist on managing the apneic child.

diagnoses: Older adult needing comprehensive geriatric assessment

cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Brown Bag Simulation to Improve Medication Management in Older Adults
presentations: medication reconciliation with a brown bag of medications

cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.brief: A transgender patient is brought to the emergency department after a workplace assault. Interprofessional teams critique the initial ED interaction, then hold a team huddle and discharge planning meeting with a standardized patient.

cases.title: Insomnia Telemedicine OSCE (TeleOSCE): A Simulated Standardized Patient Video-Visit Case for Clerkship Students
diagnoses: Depression with insomnia in a rural setting

cases.learners: pediatrics clerkship medical students, genetic counseling students

cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.title: Comprehensive Curriculum for Internal Medicine Residents on Primary Care of Patients Identifying as Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, or Transgender
diagnoses: LGBT (lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender) patient primary care

cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

cases.brief: Students receive a patient scenario about headache and discuss its management. They compare migraine drugs, mechanisms, interactions, and routes of administration.

cases.brief: An anesthesiology resident manages intraoperative sepsis progressing to septic shock. Learners recognize the need for invasive lines, fluid resuscitation, blood cultures, antibiotics, and staying intubated.

cases.license: Free for teaching; each publication states its license (most are Creative Commons)

diagnoses: Patients with limited English proficiency in oral health care
