cases.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A 60-year-old man with four days of belly pain from cholangitis arrives in septic shock at a community hospital. Learners find the source, start broad antibiotics and give fluids and vasopressors.

cases.title: Nightmares Case 2: Pneumonia
cases.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A 64-year-old man in hospital for three days with community-acquired pneumonia is getting more short of breath despite antibiotics. New residents reassess a deteriorating ward patient and escalate care.

cases.title: Bronchiolitis
cases.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A 6-month-old girl with a cold from an older sibling now has noisy breathing and is not feeding. Learners assess and support an infant with bronchiolitis and review which treatments help.

cases.title: Alcohol and opioid use
cases.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A 29-year-old man falls in the shower while drunk and cannot remember the event. After the trauma work-up, learners use screening, brief intervention and referral to treatment (SBIRT) with a live patient conversation.

cases.title: Acetaminophen Overdose with an Uncooperative Patient
cases.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A 25-year-old man took a large acetaminophen overdose to end his life and is irritable and refuses treatment. Learners treat the poisoning while addressing suicide risk, capacity and mental health law.

cases.title: Tricyclic Antidepressant Overdose
cases.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A 27-year-old man has an intentional amitriptyline overdose with a wide QRS and later cardiac arrest. Learners give sodium bicarbonate and manage a toxic arrest.

cases.title: MVC with Tension Pneumothorax
cases.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A 44-year-old driver in a highway-speed crash arrives screaming with a GCS (Glasgow Coma Scale) of 13. Learners run a primary and secondary survey and decompress a tension pneumothorax without waiting for imaging.

cases.title: Pediatric Polytrauma
cases.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A 2.5-year-old falls 9 m from a balcony and arrives at a community hospital in compensated shock, with upset family present. Learners coordinate a pediatric trauma survey and resuscitation under stress.

cases.title: Pediatric Traumatic Brain Injury
cases.authors: De Santis D, Klowak JA, Ngo Q
cases.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
cases.brief: An 18-month-old falls from a play structure, loses consciousness and is irritable with an obvious head injury. Learners manage severe pediatric head injury and raised brain pressure.

cases.title: Organophosphate Poisoning
cases.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A 60-year-old berry farmer who hand-sprayed pesticide has vomiting, diarrhea, copious secretions, slow heart rate and low oxygen. Learners recognize the cholinergic toxidrome and give atropine and pralidoxime.

cases.title: Subarachnoid Hemorrhage with Increased Intracranial Pressure
cases.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A 45-year-old man collapses at the gym after a sudden severe headache and arrives unconscious. Learners control blood pressure, intubate safely and treat raised brain pressure from a brain bleed.

cases.title: Ruptured Ectopic
cases.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A 26-year-old recent immigrant from Cambodia with limited English faints at home after days of vomiting. Learners check a pregnancy test in any young woman with syncope and resuscitate internal bleeding from ectopic pregnancy.

cases.title: Pregnant Cardiomyopathy
cases.license: CC BY-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A 38-year-old woman at 36 weeks with weeks of ignored symptoms faints at home and is in acute heart failure. Learners manage pregnancy-related cardiomyopathy and plan care for mother and baby.

cases.title: International Pediatric Emergency Medicine and Critical Care Fellow Education: Utilizing Virtual Resuscitation Simulation in Settings With Differing Resources (Case 1: Joseph, diarrhea and hypovolemic shock)
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: Joseph, 3 years old, comes to a rural clinic in Kenya after seven days of watery diarrhea and is in shock. Learners use the WHO (World Health Organization) shock definition, check dehydration and malnutrition, give fluids and glucose and decide on referral.

cases.title: International Pediatric Emergency Medicine and Critical Care Fellow Education: Utilizing Virtual Resuscitation Simulation in Settings With Differing Resources (Case 2: Stephen, diarrhea with electrolyte derangement)
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: Stephen, 2 years old, arrives at a district hospital with eight days of profuse watery diarrhea and shock; labs show high sodium and low potassium. If the salts are not corrected he goes into pulseless VT (ventricular tachycardia), so learners practice fluids, electrolyte correction, CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation) and defibrillation.

cases.title: International Pediatric Emergency Medicine and Critical Care Fellow Education: Utilizing Virtual Resuscitation Simulation in Settings With Differing Resources (Case 3: Jane, fever and septic shock)
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: Jane, 12 months old, has five days of fever and one day of lethargy and meets the WHO (World Health Organization) definition of shock at a central hospital. Learners give fluids, oxygen and antibiotics and then manage fluid overload that leads to intubation.

cases.title: A Simulation Scenario Focused on Resuscitation of a Young Infant (Neonate) for Nurses and Midwives in Malawi, a Limited Resource Country
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: Nana, a 7-week-old girl sent from the under-five clinic, looks unwell and has noisy breathing. Nursing and midwifery students in Malawi practice ABC assessment, bag-mask ventilation, CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation) and post-resuscitation care with local low-cost equipment.

cases.title: Postpartum Magnesium Sulfate Overdose: A Multidisciplinary and Interprofessional Simulation Scenario
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: A postpartum woman with preeclampsia on magnesium sulfate for seizure prevention develops magnesium toxicity and stops breathing. Obstetric, anesthesia and nursing teams practice recognizing toxicity, giving calcium and supporting breathing.

cases.title: Effectiveness of Simulation-Based Training of Undergraduate Medical Students Regarding the Management of Eclampsia: A Randomized Controlled Educational Trial
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A trial at AIIMS (All India Institute of Medical Sciences) Hyderabad, India, built and tested a simulation module on managing an eclamptic seizure. It gives a tested eclampsia training design for undergraduate medical students in an Indian teaching hospital.

cases.title: Impact of an Obstetrical Emergency Simulation Learning Module on Midwifery Students' Competency: A Non-randomized Control Study
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A study from Chennai, India, used five staged simulation scenarios (eclampsia, antepartum hemorrhage, cord prolapse, prolonged labor and postpartum hemorrhage) with 16 OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination: a timed exam station where a student sees a standardized patient) stations for midwifery students. It aligns with Indian Nursing Council and WHO (World Health Organization) skilled birth attendant guidance.

cases.title: Pediatric Rattlesnake Envenomation: A Simulation Scenario With Optional Health Equity, Virtual Facilitation, and Senior Learner Modifications
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: Carlos, a 3-year-old boy at a campsite, comes in crying and holding his arm after an unwitnessed snakebite. Learners recognize envenomation, give antivenom and treat an antivenom reaction, with optional health equity and virtual versions.

cases.title: Pediatric Motor Vehicle-Pedestrian Accident: a Simulation Scenario for Emergency Medicine Trainees
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: An 8-year-old boy struck by a pick-up truck arrives at a rural emergency department with femur and elbow fractures, 90 minutes from a trauma center. Learners run pediatric trauma care and arrange transfer.

cases.title: Prehospital Trauma Care: A Simulation Scenario for Rural-Based Healthcare Providers
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: A two-vehicle crash on a rural highway 80 km from hospital leaves several casualties, some ejected. Rural providers practice scene safety, triage and stabilization before transport.

cases.title: Initial Resuscitation of a Multisystem Trauma Patient Following a Fall From Height: A Complete Simulation Scenario for Medical Students
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: A 25-year-old man falls 20 feet and has an open femur fracture, bleeding, tension pneumothorax and head injury. Medical students practice the primary survey and early trauma resuscitation.

cases.title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis: An Emergency Medicine Simulation Scenario
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: A 19-year-old man in his first weekend at a university dormitory is found with vomiting, weakness and low consciousness, with few details known. Learners diagnose new diabetic ketoacidosis and manage fluids, insulin and potassium.

cases.title: Two Simulation Cases to Prepare for a Public Festival: Pediatric Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) Ingestion and Alcohol Toxicity
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: A 15-year-old is found lying on the ground at a hot summer music festival, drunk with slurred speech, with an older sibling present (a second case covers MDMA toxicity). Staff practice medical care of intoxication and the social and safeguarding side of the case.

cases.title: Chest Pain on the Ward: A Simulation Scenario for Rural Family and Emergency Medicine Trainees
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: A patient admitted earlier in the day at a rural hospital develops chest pain on the ward and goes into cardiogenic shock from acute coronary syndrome. Rural family and emergency trainees practice recognition and stabilization.

cases.title: Diagnosis and Management of an Inferior ST-elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Simulation Scenario
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: A 51-year-old has two hours of epigastric pain that antacids do not help. Learners recognize an inferior STEMI (ST-elevation myocardial infarction), treat it and follow ACLS (Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support) if it deteriorates.

cases.title: Necrotizing Fasciitis: An Emergency Medicine Simulation Scenario
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: A 68-year-old woman who fell during yard work the day before has hip pain and is becoming septic. Learners diagnose necrotizing fasciitis, start treatment and advocate for surgery when consultants push back.

cases.title: Simulation of an Atypical Presentation of Necrotizing Enterocolitis in the Emergency Department
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: A term newborn comes to the emergency center with bowel inflammation (necrotizing enterocolitis) caused by a urinary infection and bloodstream infection. Learners recognize a septic infant and resuscitate with PALS (Pediatric Advanced Life Support).

cases.title: Asthma Exacerbation: An Emergency Medicine Simulation Scenario
cases.license: CC BY 3.0
cases.brief: A 23-year-old woman with asthma and past ICU (intensive care unit) admissions comes in short of breath after a recent course of prednisone. Learners manage a severe asthma attack, with difficulty adjusted to the learner level.

cases.title: EM ReSCu Peds: Case 5 | Diabetic Ketoacidosis
cases.license: Free access; ALiEM content All Rights Reserved
cases.brief: An 8-year-old girl lies miserable with vomiting and belly pain and dry lips, with an anxious mother at the bedside. Learners diagnose pediatric DKA (diabetic ketoacidosis) and manage fluids and insulin safely.

cases.title: EM ReSCu Peds: Case 13 | Pneumonia and Septic Shock
cases.license: Free access; ALiEM content All Rights Reserved
cases.brief: A 10-year-old boy with a tracheostomy has had a week of cough and fever and now cannot keep his oxygen above 85%. Learners manage pneumonia with septic shock and airway problems in a medically complex child.

cases.title: EM ReSCu Peds: Case 9 | Neonatal Delivery
cases.authors: Tay KY, Sanseau E, Carr L
cases.license: Free access; ALiEM content All Rights Reserved
cases.brief: A mother arrives in the emergency department and the newborn of unknown gestational age is limp, blue and not breathing. Learners run neonatal resuscitation from the first minute.

cases.title: EM ReSCu Peds: Case 7 | Multisystem Trauma
cases.license: Free access; ALiEM content All Rights Reserved
cases.brief: A 6-year-old girl ran into the street after a ball and was hit by a car; she has slow shallow breathing and a deformed leg. Learners run a pediatric trauma resuscitation.

cases.title: EM ReSCu Peds: Case 14 | Status Asthmaticus
cases.license: Free access; ALiEM content All Rights Reserved
cases.brief: A 6-year-old boy is quiet, in severe respiratory distress with poor air entry. Learners escalate treatment for life-threatening asthma.

cases.title: SimBox: A Postpartum Complication
cases.authors: Athanasopoulou S, Cohen S, Auerbach M, Kou M, Sanseau E
cases.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
cases.brief: A 16-year-old who did not know she was pregnant arrives by ambulance in active labor with vaginal bleeding. The emergency team manages postpartum hemorrhage and decides where to transfer.

cases.title: SimBox: Newborn Resuscitation
cases.license: unknown (free download)
cases.brief: A 16-year-old in active labor who learned of her pregnancy that day delivers in the emergency department. The team resuscitates the newborn, with a low-cost doll or mannequin and a video monitor.

cases.title: SimBox: A Sick Neonate (Neonatal Shock)
cases.license: unknown (free download)
cases.brief: A 7-day-old term baby boy is brought in by ambulance lethargic and very unwell. The team treats neonatal shock with fluids, glucose, warmth and antibiotics and works through causes including sepsis and heart disease.

cases.title: SimBox: Infant with Respiratory Distress (Bronchiolitis)
cases.license: unknown (free download)
cases.brief: A 4-month-old boy has four days of cough, congestion and poor feeding, breathing at 80 per minute with oxygen at 86%. The team supports breathing in bronchiolitis and plans transfer.

cases.title: SimBox: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)
cases.license: unknown (free download)
cases.brief: A previously healthy 10-year-old girl with weeks of thirst and frequent urination is sleepy and pale with slow capillary refill. The team diagnoses DKA (diabetic ketoacidosis) and starts evidence-based treatment.

cases.title: SimBox: Suicide Risk Assessment
cases.authors: Mielke B, Hilliard M, Simpson L, Brenner A
cases.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
cases.brief: A 12-year-old girl seen for abdominal pain screens at moderate suicide risk. Clinicians practice a full suicide risk assessment (SAFE-T (Suicide Assessment Five-step Evaluation and Triage) or BSSA), set the risk level and build a safety plan.

cases.title: SimBox: Suicide Screen - Nursing
cases.authors: Mielke B, Brenner A, Hilliard M, Simpson L
cases.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
cases.brief: A 12-year-old girl arrives at triage with abdominal pain and poor appetite. Nurses practice asking the suicide screening questions (ASQ or C-SSRS (Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale)), handling barriers and acting on a positive screen.

cases.title: SimBox: Severe Head Injury
cases.license: unknown (free download)
cases.brief: A 5-year-old boy who was not properly restrained in a high-speed car crash has a scalp hematoma and then a large epidural bleed. The team scores his mental state, intubates and treats raised brain pressure.

cases.title: COPD exacerbation assessment and intervention
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A client has an acute COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) exacerbation. Nursing students do priority assessments and start care based on RNAO COPD guidelines.

cases.title: Acute Depression
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A patient with acute depression and suicidal thoughts has been admitted voluntarily to a psychiatric unit. Nursing students practice a trauma-informed interview, mental status exam and suicide risk assessment in a virtual patient.

cases.title: Assessing Suicide Risk & Responding
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A virtual patient has suicidal thoughts. Nursing students use the SAFE-T (Suicide Assessment Five-step Evaluation and Triage) protocol with the C-SSRS (Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale) to judge risk, share safety concerns with the team and make a safe care plan.

cases.title: Pediatric Sepsis ("Harper Peterson")
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
cases.brief: A critically ill infant needs paramedic stabilization before transport. Paramedic students recognize septic shock, treat circulatory failure and decide when to intubate.

cases.title: Congenital cerebral malaria: a masquerader in a neonate
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 5-day-old baby in Nigeria looks like he has neonatal sepsis, jaundice and then meningitis, but a blood film shows malaria parasites. Learners practice a neonatal fever workup and remember to test for malaria in newborns in endemic areas.

cases.title: Poor response to artesunate treatment in two patients with severe malaria on the Thai-Myanmar border
cases.learner: Residents, internal medicine and ID trainees
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: Two adults with severe falciparum malaria on the Thai-Myanmar border respond poorly to IV (intravenous) artesunate; one dies and one clears parasites only after 11 days. Learners recognize severe malaria, monitor parasite clearance and think about artemisinin resistance.
cases.learners: Residents, internal medicine and ID trainees

cases.title: Duodenal perforation in a 12-month old child with severe malaria
cases.license: CC BY (Creative Commons Attribution License)
cases.brief: A 1-year-old in Ghana with confirmed severe malaria also has a perforated duodenal ulcer, and the malaria result delays the surgical diagnosis. Learners practice keeping a wide differential when a febrile child has a positive malaria test.

cases.title: Severe retinal whitening in an adult with cerebral malaria
cases.license: ASTMH re-use licence (non-commercial use with citation)
cases.brief: A retinal photo of a 24-year-old Bangladeshi man with non-fatal cerebral malaria shows severe malarial retinopathy. Use it as an exam finding card when an SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) portrays a comatose patient with cerebral malaria.

cases.title: Plasmodium vivax cerebral malaria in an adult patient in Sudan
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 60-year-old man in Khartoum develops cerebral malaria caused by P. vivax, not P. falciparum. Learners learn that vivax can be severe and that species testing matters in Africa.

cases.title: Gorgas Case 2025-9 (uncomplicated Plasmodium vivax malaria)
cases.authors: Gorgas Course, UAB and Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia
cases.license: Free access; no open licence stated
cases.brief: An 18-year-old woman comes to a Lima emergency department with 5 days of fever, chills, headache and dark urine. Learners take a travel and exposure history and confirm malaria with a rapid test and blood smear.

cases.title: An 11-month-old boy with tuberculous meningitis presenting as progressive limb weakness, fever, developmental retardation, and loss of consciousness: a case report
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: An 11-month-old boy in Iran loses milestones and develops limb weakness, fever and reduced consciousness over weeks, and is treated successfully for TB (tuberculosis) meningitis. Learners take a developmental and TB contact history from a parent and recognize subacute meningitis.

cases.title: Use of alternative cerebrospinal fluid-based biomarkers to help diagnose Xpert-negative tuberculous meningitis: A case report
cases.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
cases.brief: A 5-year-old boy in Nepal has 2 weeks of evening fever, headache and vomiting, then a seizure and left-sided weakness while on antibiotics for presumed bacterial meningitis. Learners see that a negative Xpert test does not rule out TB (tuberculosis) meningitis and use CSF (cerebrospinal fluid) markers to decide.

cases.title: Drug-resistant tuberculosis treatment complicated by antiretroviral resistance in HIV coinfected patients: a report of six cases in Lesotho
cases.learner: Residents, HIV and TB program clinicians
cases.license: Free to read; copyright ASTMH
cases.brief: Six patients in Lesotho on drug-resistant TB (tuberculosis) treatment also have HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) that no longer responds to their antiretroviral drugs. Learners plan care for MDR-TB (multidrug-resistant tuberculosis) with HIV where viral load and resistance tests are scarce.
cases.learners: Residents, HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) and TB (tuberculosis) program clinicians

cases.title: Lung abscess complicating a case of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 54-year-old man in India who stopped TB (tuberculosis) treatment after 2 months returns with blood-tinged sputum and a cavity with a lung abscess, later found to be MDR-TB (multidrug-resistant tuberculosis). Learners explore reasons for stopping treatment and counsel on adherence.

cases.title: Gorgas Case 2026-11 (Pott's disease)
cases.authors: Gorgas Course, UAB and Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia
cases.license: Free access; no open licence stated
cases.brief: A 39-year-old man from Barranca, Peru, has 10 months of back pain, a growing back mass, weight loss, night sweats, cough and then leg weakness. Learners link back pain and red flags to spinal TB (tuberculosis) and ask about TB treatment history.

cases.title: Self-Study Module 4: Treatment of Latent Tuberculosis Infection and Tuberculosis Disease (case studies 4.1 to 4.7)
cases.learner: Nurses, medical students, community health workers
cases.license: Public domain (US government work)
cases.brief: Short case studies include a household contact visit, a drinker on isoniazid, a toddler with TB (tuberculosis) meningitis and a patient worried that her urine has changed color. Each is a ready prompt for a brief treatment counseling role-play with an answer key.
cases.learners: Nurses, medical students, community health workers

cases.title: Self-Study Module 6: Managing Tuberculosis Patients and Improving Adherence (case studies 6.1 to 6.6)
cases.learner: Nurses, case managers, community health workers
cases.license: Public domain (US government work)
cases.brief: Case studies include a restaurant cook newly diagnosed with smear-positive TB (tuberculosis) and a recent immigrant from India who starts missing directly observed therapy. Learners assess beliefs about TB and solve adherence barriers.
cases.learners: Nurses, case managers, community health workers

cases.title: Tuberculosis Radiology Practice Cases
cases.authors: Curry International Tuberculosis Center and Firland Northwest TB Center
cases.license: Free access; copyright Regents of the University of California
cases.brief: Brief interactive cases where learners find abnormal areas on chest X-rays in real clinical scenarios. Use the images as investigation results inside a TB (tuberculosis) SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) station.

cases.title: Evaluation of a Headache in Advanced HIV (Case Discussions, Season 1 Episode 2)
cases.license: Free access; copyright University of Washington
cases.brief: A 28-year-old man newly diagnosed with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) and a CD4 count of 4 has 2 weeks of headache, photophobia, blurred vision and vomiting. Learners recognize possible cryptococcal meningitis and plan urgent imaging and lumbar puncture; a follow-up episode covers treatment.

cases.title: Evaluation of Focal Neurological Symptoms in a Patient with Advanced HIV (Case Discussions, Season 1 Episode 7)
cases.license: Free access; copyright University of Washington
cases.brief: A 27-year-old man with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) has a headache that started 2 to 3 weeks ago and new focal neurological symptoms. Learners build a differential for brain lesions in advanced HIV, including toxoplasmosis.

cases.title: Ischemic stroke as a complication of cryptococcal meningitis and immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome: a case report
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 38-year-old man in Blantyre, Malawi, newly diagnosed with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus), has 2 weeks of headache and vomiting and is treated for cryptococcal meningitis, then has a stroke after starting ART (antiretroviral therapy). Learners manage raised CSF (cerebrospinal fluid) pressure and recognize IRIS.

cases.title: Cryptococcal meningitis and immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome in a pediatric patient with HIV after switching to second line antiretroviral therapy: a case report
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 10-year-old girl with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) in Uganda develops severe headache and seizures 8 weeks after switching to second-line ART (antiretroviral therapy), and has cryptococcal meningitis. Learners take a pediatric HIV treatment history with a caregiver and recognize IRIS.
cases.learners: Pediatric trainees, HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) clinic staff

cases.title: Acute vision loss in post-partum period as presenting symptom of HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis: an unusual case report
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 25-year-old woman in India loses vision in both eyes after giving birth and is found to have HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) and cryptococcal meningitis. Learners widen the differential for postpartum neurological symptoms and handle a new HIV diagnosis sensitively.

cases.title: Pulmonary cryptococcosis presenting as acute severe respiratory distress in a newly diagnosed HIV patient in Tanzania: a case report
cases.license: CC BY-NC
cases.brief: A patient newly diagnosed with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) in Mwanza, Tanzania, has severe breathing difficulty and dies after pulmonary cryptococcosis is missed. Learners think beyond TB (tuberculosis) and PCP when a patient with advanced HIV is short of breath.

cases.title: Gorgas Case 2023-04 (presumptive dengue without alarm signs)
cases.authors: Gorgas Course, UAB and Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia
cases.license: Free access; no open licence stated
cases.brief: A 20-year-old medical student has 7 days of high fever, headache, eye pain, joint pain and a spreading rash after a trip home to the Peruvian jungle. Learners take a travel history, check for warning signs and rule out malaria.

cases.title: Dengue shock syndrome complicated with acute liver failure and kidney injury, infective endocarditis, and deep vein thrombosis: a case report
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 38-year-old woman in Colombo, Sri Lanka, develops dengue shock with liver and kidney failure and later bacterial complications. Learners practice fluid management and close monitoring in the critical phase of dengue.

cases.title: Expanded dengue syndrome presenting with acute liver failure, acute kidney injury, pancreatic involvement, coagulopathy, and multiple intracranial hemorrhages in a young child: a case report
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 6-year-old girl in Sri Lanka has 5 days of fever, bloody diarrhea, blood in the urine and a swollen knee, and develops multi-organ dengue. Learners recognize warning signs in a child and escalate care early.

cases.title: Case Report: Dengue Fever Progressing to Acute Liver Failure and Hepatic Encephalopathy
cases.license: Free to read; copyright ASTMH
cases.brief: A young man in Indore, India, with dengue develops liver failure and confusion without shock. Learners see that dengue can present with severe organ involvement and learn which tests to follow.

cases.title: Case Report: Typhoid Fever Complicated by Ileal Perforation in an Urban Slum of Dhaka, Bangladesh
cases.learner: Medical students, surgical and medicine trainees
cases.license: CC BY-NC 4.0
cases.brief: A 19-year-old man in a Dhaka urban slum has high fever, lower abdominal pain and vomiting, and has a typhoid ileal perforation. Learners recognize an acute abdomen in typhoid and plan urgent surgery and antibiotics.
cases.learners: Medical students, surgical and medicine trainees

cases.title: Severe thrombocytopenia in a child with typhoid fever: a case report
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 4-year-old boy returning from travel has a long fever and a very low platelet count, and blood culture shows typhoid. Learners take a travel and food history from a parent and manage low platelets without transfusion.

cases.title: A case of typhoid fever with neurological presentation
cases.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
cases.brief: A 31-year-old man in Dhaka has 18 days of fever, headache, rash, diarrhea, confusion and blurred vision, with sixth nerve palsies. Learners include typhoid in the differential of prolonged fever with neurological signs.

cases.title: Fatal case of meningococcal meningitis in a child from rural Bhutan: A case report
cases.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
cases.brief: A 10-year-old boy in rural Bhutan comes home from school with fever and body aches, becomes drowsy overnight and has a purpuric rash. Learners recognize meningococcal disease fast, give antibiotics before transfer and notify public health.

cases.title: Presumed Meningococcal meningitis with Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome from a rural Ethiopia: a fatal case report and literature review
cases.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (Annals of Medicine and Surgery)
cases.brief: An unvaccinated 35-year-old woman in rural Ethiopia has 24 hours of fever, headache and neck pain, then confusion, low blood pressure and a spreading purpuric rash. Learners manage septic shock with meningitis in a low-resource hospital.

cases.title: Disseminated melioidosis: challenge to routine antibiotic therapy: a case report
cases.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
cases.brief: A middle-aged man with diabetes in Raipur, India, has high fever, breathlessness and a swollen knee and ankle, first misdiagnosed as TB (tuberculosis). Learners consider melioidosis in septic diabetic patients in South and Southeast Asia.

cases.title: Amoebic Dysentery Complicated by Hypovolemic Shock and Sepsis in an Infant with Severe Acute Malnutrition: A Case Report
cases.license: CC BY 4.0 (Microorganisms)
cases.brief: A 10-month-old boy with severe acute malnutrition is admitted in Port Sudan with bloody diarrhea, shock and sepsis. Learners apply careful fluid and antibiotic rules for malnourished children with diarrhea.

cases.title: Optimizing survival in Russell's viper bite cases in low-resource setting: two case reports
cases.learner: Medical students, emergency and medicine trainees
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: Two men in rural Bangladesh go to traditional healers after Russell's viper bites and arrive late with bleeding problems and kidney failure. Learners take a bite history, run a 20-minute clotting test and plan antivenom and dialysis.
cases.learners: Medical students, emergency and medicine trainees

cases.title: Confirmed Ceylon krait (Bungarus ceylonicus) envenoming in Sri Lanka resulting in neuromuscular paralysis: a case report
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 26-year-old man in Sri Lanka bitten by a krait develops droopy eyelids, eye movement weakness, facial weakness and trouble swallowing. Learners check for neurotoxic signs and watch for breathing failure.

cases.title: Priapism following a juvenile Russell's viper bite: An unusual case report
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 16-year-old boy in India develops a painful erection soon after a Russell's viper bite, which settles after antivenom. Learners handle a sensitive history with an adolescent and recognize systemic envenoming.

cases.title: Vibrio vulnificus sepsis following Naja atra Snakebite: A rare case report from Vietnam
cases.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
cases.brief: An 80-year-old woman collecting fish on the coast of Thai Binh, Vietnam, is bitten by a cobra and arrives 18 hours later with tissue death and septic shock. Learners combine antivenom, antibiotics, dialysis and surgery.
cases.learners: Residents, ICU (intensive care unit) and surgical trainees

cases.title: Shortcomings in snake bite management in rural Cameroon: a case report
cases.license: CC BY 4.0 (BMC Research Notes)
cases.brief: A 10-year-old boy from a remote area of Cameroon arrives 12 hours after a snakebite to the face with severe envenoming, and antivenom is out of stock. Learners manage envenoming with limited antivenom and talk with the family about delays in care.

cases.title: Revered but Poorly Understood: A Case Report of Dendroaspis polylepis (Black Mamba) Envenomation in Watamu, Malindi Kenya, and a Review of the Literature
