cases.brief: Judy, 85, has mild dementia and is admitted with pneumonia and new atrial fibrillation; her daughter Karen, her carer, shows strain. Learners tell delirium from dementia with Mini-Cog and CAM (Confusion Assessment Method), use non-drug approaches to behavior, and plan discharge.
cases.learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

cases.title: Butch Sampson (ACE.V veterans unfolding case)
cases.learner: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners
cases.license: Free to download for teaching; copyright National League for Nursing (no open license stated)
cases.brief: Butch, 68, is a homeless veteran with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes and an infected toe who needs surgery. Learners assess the wound, teach about diet and medicines, and plan discharge around housing and other social needs.
cases.learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

cases.title: Eugene Shaw (ACE.V veterans unfolding case)
cases.learner: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners
cases.license: Free to download for teaching; copyright National League for Nursing (no open license stated)
cases.brief: Eugene, 87, a Korean War veteran with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, tobacco and alcohol use, has leg pain from a blocked artery and needs bypass surgery. Learners give pre- and post-operative care, check medicine adherence and plan lifestyle change at discharge.
cases.learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

cases.title: Jenny Brown (ACE.V veterans unfolding case)
cases.learner: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners
cases.license: Free to download for teaching; copyright National League for Nursing (no open license stated)
cases.brief: Jenny, 29, is a pregnant Iraq veteran admitted with severe anxiety after learning her baby will have a cleft lip and palate; the case follows her through antenatal and postpartum care. Learners screen for anxiety, depression, suicide risk, PTSD (post-traumatic stress disorder) and brain injury.
cases.learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

cases.title: Randy Adams (ACE.V veterans unfolding case)
cases.learner: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners
cases.license: Free to download for teaching; copyright National League for Nursing (no open license stated)
cases.brief: Randy, 32, an Iraq veteran with PTSD (post-traumatic stress disorder) and headaches, comes to the emergency department confused after a car crash. Learners assess mental and neurological status, review PTSD treatment and support him and his family over several weeks.
cases.learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

cases.title: Patrick and Gloria Lake (ACE.D disabilities unfolding case)
cases.authors: Mariani B, Meakim C, Smeltzer S
cases.learner: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners
cases.license: Free to download for teaching; copyright National League for Nursing (no open license stated)
cases.brief: Patrick, 64, has an above-knee amputation from a war injury, arthritis and heart failure; he is seen in clinic, admitted for heart failure, then followed at home. Learners practice respectful communication with a person with a disability, focused assessment and patient teaching.
cases.learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

cases.title: Mary Lou and Rob Brady (ACE.D disabilities unfolding case)
cases.authors: Meakim C, Mariani B, Meyers S, Smeltzer SC
cases.learner: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners
cases.license: Free to download for teaching; copyright National League for Nursing (no open license stated)
cases.brief: Mary Lou has a stroke at 20; the case follows her through rehabilitation, a pregnancy at 26 with left-sided weakness, and discharge after a cesarean birth. Learners do neurological and psychosocial assessment and plan safe discharge for a mother with a disability.
cases.learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

cases.title: mhGAP Depression module role plays (assessment and management)
cases.learner: Non-specialist primary care workers (doctors, nurses, clinical officers)
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A person comes to a health center feeling sad and exhausted for two months, sleeping badly and afraid of losing their job; one version is a 27-year-old who lost his bank job after a broken engagement. Learners use the mhGAP (WHO Mental Health Gap Action Programme) guide to assess for depression, rule out other causes such as past mania or thyroid disease, and plan care.
cases.learners: Non-specialist primary care workers (doctors, nurses, clinical officers)

cases.title: mhGAP Self-harm/suicide module role plays
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Scripts include a 30-year-old woman with postnatal depression recovering on the ward after drinking pesticide, and an 18-year-old woman who cut her arms after a fight with her father. Learners practice asking directly about suicide, assessing risk and planning psychosocial follow-up.

cases.title: mhGAP Alcohol and drug use module role plays
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: One patient returns after a hypertension diagnosis and drinks 10 to 12 drinks a day with shaking when he stops; another, Mr Sana, is a weekend binge drinker worried about blackouts. Learners assess alcohol use with the mhGAP (WHO Mental Health Gap Action Programme) algorithm and use brief motivational interviewing.

cases.title: mhGAP Dementia module role plays (assessment and follow-up)
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Farah brings her mother Ingrid, 73, who is forgetful, struggles with cooking and word finding, and later wanders at night and falls. Learners assess the person and the carer for dementia, then manage behavior, safety and carer stress at follow-up.

cases.title: NAC Examination sample case study: Stan Mortensen
cases.learner: International medical graduates and final-year medical students
cases.license: Free for exam preparation; copyright Medical Council of Canada
cases.brief: Stan, 51, a busy store owner, was told he had diabetes six months ago, ran out of metformin and now has a random glucose of 12 mmol/L. In 11 minutes the candidate takes a focused history and counsels him on management options.
cases.learners: International medical graduates and final-year medical students

cases.title: NAC Examination sample case study: Sandrine Thomas
cases.learner: International medical graduates and final-year medical students
cases.license: Free for exam preparation; copyright Medical Council of Canada
cases.brief: Sandrine, 45, a chef, needs foot surgery and is afraid that opioid pain medicine will make her relapse after past drug use 10 years ago. The candidate takes a focused history, makes a safe discharge pain plan and counsels her.
cases.learners: International medical graduates and final-year medical students

cases.title: Assessing suicide risk and responding
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (free Simulation Canada account needed to download)
cases.brief: A virtual patient needs a mental health and suicide risk assessment. Learners use the SAFE-T (Suicide Assessment Five-step Evaluation and Triage) protocol with the Columbia scale, identify warning signs and protective factors, and make a safe care plan.

cases.title: Acute stroke assessment
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (free Simulation Canada account needed to download)
cases.brief: A patient with an acute stroke, played by a patient actor or a high-fidelity manikin. Learners assess the patient with the Canadian Neurological Scale, based on Canadian stroke best practice guidance.

cases.title: Neonatal resuscitation and surfactant administration
cases.authors: Herman H, Armstrong K, Bassant M
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (free Simulation Canada account needed to download)
cases.brief: A 34-year-old mother with preeclampsia and threatened preterm labor has an emergency cesarean birth, and the preterm baby needs help to breathe. Learners work with the team to resuscitate and stabilize the newborn and give surfactant.

cases.title: Delirium
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (free Simulation Canada account needed to download)
cases.brief: A 79-year-old with hypertension and mild dementia is two days after hip fracture surgery. Learners recognize delirium on top of dementia in an extended reality simulation.

cases.title: Post-Partum Mental Health
cases.learner: Nursing students in maternal-child or mental health practice
cases.license: Free open access (no membership); no license stated on the page
cases.brief: Willow, 32, a first-time mother with schizoaffective disorder, is 26 hours after birth; her small baby may show withdrawal from her medicines and substance use. Learners assess physical and psychosocial needs and act using trauma- and violence-informed care.
cases.learners: Nursing students in maternal-child or mental health practice

cases.title: Interprofessional Collaboration: Delirium, Dementia and Decision-Making
cases.learner: Nursing and other health learners and practitioners
cases.license: Free open access (no membership); no license stated on the page
cases.brief: Clay, an older farmer who values his independence, has cognitive decline and is in hospital with a complicated urinary infection that affects his thinking. Learners tell delirium from dementia and use shared, ethical decision-making with him and his family.
cases.learners: Nursing and other health learners and practitioners

cases.title: Deteriorating Patient: Septic Shock
cases.license: Free open access (no membership); no license stated on the page
cases.brief: Nicolas, 55, with type 2 diabetes and hypertension, is three days after appendix surgery and now confused with abnormal lung and abdominal findings. Learners recognize sepsis and septic shock early and act; English and French versions and in-person PDF versions exist.

cases.title: Care of the Older Adult with Urosepsis
cases.license: Free open access (no membership); no license stated on the page
cases.brief: Mr Sarazin, an older man with a urinary catheter, comes from the emergency department with two days of worsening confusion and agitation. Learners assess and treat a patient who is getting worse from urosepsis.

cases.title: Acute Heart Failure with Next Gen Questions
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: Mr Fernandez, 62, a retired veteran with chronic heart failure who moved to a nursing home after falls, is admitted to the cardiac unit for dehydration and becomes short of breath. Learners work through the chart, x-ray and NCLEX (the US nursing licensing exam) Next Generation style clinical judgment questions.

cases.title: Heart Failure Patient in a Long-Term Care Facility
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 62-year-old man with heart failure lives in a long-term care facility. Learners notice changes, assess him and decide on the nurse's next actions.

cases.title: Patient with Heart Failure on a Ventilator
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 62-year-old man with heart failure is on a mechanical ventilator. Learners assess him, respond to changes and practice safe care of a ventilated patient.

cases.title: Administering Cardiac Medication to a Patient with Dementia
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: Mr Johnson, 87, lives in long-term care with dementia, hypertension, atrial fibrillation and chronic renal failure. Learners give his heart medicines safely, check the right assessments first and communicate with a confused patient.

cases.title: Clinic Walk-In with Chronic Angina
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: A 69-year-old man with chronic stable angina walks into his family practice clinic and asks to speak to a nurse. Learners choose the priority questions and actions for possible cardiac chest pain.

cases.title: Therapeutic Communication: Domestic Violence
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: Allison, 32, a mother of two in a rural community, has come to the emergency department five times this year with bruising typical of partner violence. Learners practice therapeutic communication, screening and safe referral, including to a social worker.

cases.title: Therapeutic Communication: End of Life
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: Laura, 35, has end-stage lung cancer spread to bone and brain and chose hospice, but her mother does not agree; she is admitted for comfort care. Learners practice therapeutic communication with the patient and family at the end of life.

cases.title: Andy Dufrayne (video virtual patient)
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0
cases.brief: Andy, 79, is admitted to hospital with COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). Learners explore the ethics and results of choices about his do-not-attempt-resuscitation status and his capacity to decide.

cases.title: Derek Bryant Tutorial 1 (virtual patient)
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0
cases.brief: Derek, 71, lives in a residential home and sees his GP with abdominal pain and passing small amounts of very concentrated urine; he has diabetes and hypertension. Learners work through the diagnosis in an older patient with several conditions.

cases.title: Standardized patient TB case scenarios, Mumbai and Patna (Kwan et al.)
cases.authors: Kwan A, Daniels B, Saria V, et al.
cases.learner: Primary care providers and trainers; SP program designers
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: Four scripted SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) cases: classic cough and fever for 2 to 3 weeks, the same after failed antibiotics with an abnormal chest x-ray, a patient with a positive sputum test, and a suspected drug-resistant TB (tuberculosis) case after incomplete treatment. The cases and correct management are in Table 2, and SP script development and training are in S1 Text.
cases.learners: Primary care providers and trainers; SP (standardized patient: a trained actor who plays a patient) program designers

cases.title: SPEED trial: seven SP cases for adolescent HIV care in Kenya (Wilson et al.)
cases.authors: Wilson KS, Mugo C, Bukusi D, et al.
cases.learner: HIV clinic health workers in Kenya
cases.license: CC BY 4.0
cases.brief: Seven actor cases for youth living with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus), from a routine visit to disclosure to a 13-year-old, family planning, partner violence with alcohol use, and a 16-year-old with suicidal thoughts and poor adherence. The protocol summarizes each case; full scripts are not published, so this is a strong outline for local script writing.
cases.learners: HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) clinic health workers in Kenya

cases.title: OSCE station: announcing a breast cancer diagnosis (Polivka et al.)
cases.authors: Polivka L, Delcour C, Dufresne H, et al.
cases.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
cases.brief: A standardized patient receives the news that she has breast cancer. Additional file 1 gives the station and a 15-item grid that scores the student's communication when breaking bad news.

cases.title: BEC Module 1, Case 1: older man who collapsed and is barely breathing
cases.learner: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 70-year-old man arrives by taxi after losing consciousness mid-conversation; he vomited and now breathes only 3 times a minute. Learners practise the ABCDE (Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure) approach, airway and breathing support, and a 1 to 2 sentence handover.
cases.learners: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers

cases.title: BEC Module 1, Case 2: 2-year-old with fever, cough and trouble breathing
cases.learner: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A mother brings her 2-year-old son with 3 days of fever, heavy cough and worsening breathing; today he will not eat or drink. Learners run a paediatric ABCDE (Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure) assessment, ask the facilitator for findings and give a handover.
cases.learners: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers

cases.title: BEC Module 2, Case 1: car crash with open thigh fracture
cases.learner: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 30-year-old man lies in a taxi after a car crash, in severe pain, with blood-soaked jeans and bone sticking out of the right thigh. Learners run the trauma primary survey, control bleeding and summarize for handover.
cases.learners: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers

cases.title: BEC Module 2, Case 2: 5-year-old scalded by boiling water
cases.learner: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A boy pulled a pan of boiling water onto his right hand, arm, chest, abdomen and thigh; his mother cooled him and does not know his weight. Learners do the primary survey, estimate burn size and weight, and plan fluids and pain relief.
cases.learners: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers

cases.title: BEC Module 3, Case 1: stab wound to the chest with severe breathlessness
cases.learner: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 22-year-old man was robbed and stabbed in the left chest and now has severe difficulty breathing. Learners use ABCDE (Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure) to recognize and act on a life-threatening chest injury.
cases.learners: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers

cases.title: BEC Module 3, Case 2: 6-year-old with 3 days of noisy breathing
cases.learner: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A mother says her 6-year-old son has had trouble breathing for 3 days and makes funny noises when he breathes. Learners assess the airway and breathing, find the cause from facilitator findings and treat.
cases.learners: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers

cases.title: BEC Module 4, Case 1: man with heavy drinking, black stools and weakness
cases.learner: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 48-year-old man with a history of alcohol abuse has had very dark stools for 2 days and now cannot stand. Learners recognize shock from blood loss, start resuscitation and hand over.
cases.learners: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers

cases.title: BEC Module 4, Case 2: 4-year-old with diarrhoea, vomiting and shock
cases.learner: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A girl has had near-constant diarrhoea for 3 days and vomits everything she drinks; she may have had fever and is not malnourished. Learners assess circulation, choose and give the right fluid and reassess.
cases.learners: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers

cases.title: BEC Module 5, Case 1: confused man found at a bus stop
cases.learner: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Bystanders bring a 42-year-old stranger found slumped and very confused at a bus stop. Learners work through ABCDE (Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure) and the causes of altered mental status, including checking blood glucose.
cases.learners: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers

cases.title: BEC Module 5, Case 2: 3-year-old with high fever, two seizures and confusion
cases.learner: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A mother brings her child, wrapped in blankets, after two seizures today and 2 days of high fever and growing confusion. Learners manage seizures, fever and glucose and consider serious infection such as meningitis or cerebral malaria (the workbook does not name the diagnosis).
cases.learners: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers

cases.title: BEC Skills section, handover example 3: older man with chest pressure
cases.learner: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 75-year-old man with a past heart attack and blood pressure medicine had 30 minutes of central chest pressure while walking home carrying heavy bags; it has now stopped. The workbook uses him as a worked SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation: a handover format) handover example after aspirin and an IV (intravenous) line; learners can take the SAMPLE history and practise the handover.
cases.learners: Nurses, doctors, clinical officers and other first-contact emergency providers

cases.title: ETAT facilitator guide, Scenario 5: 4-year-old hit by a bicycle
cases.learner: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: A boy is carried in on a blanket, unconscious and with obstructed breathing, bleeding from the lower leg. Learners triage as emergency, protect the neck while opening the airway, stop bleeding and treat shock.
cases.learners: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children

cases.title: ETAT facilitator guide, Scenario 7: 3-year-old with pneumonia and shock
cases.learner: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: A pale, floppy boy has coughed for 3 days and now breathes fast with chest recession and a tracheal tug; his hands are cold with slow capillary refill. Learners give oxygen, treat shock with a fluid bolus and reassess; without oxygen he goes into respiratory arrest.
cases.learners: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children

cases.title: ETAT facilitator guide, Scenario 8: 4-month-old with fever, fast breathing and shock
cases.learner: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: A 5 kg baby has fever, fast breathing, refuses the breast and has vomited and had diarrhoea; pulses are weak and blood sugar is very low. Learners check central pulses, treat shock, give glucose and oxygen, or the baby deteriorates.
cases.learners: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children

cases.title: ETAT facilitator guide, Scenario 9: 10-month-old with 24 hours of vomiting and diarrhoea
cases.learner: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: An 8 kg baby has cold grey hands and feet, slow capillary refill and responds only to pain; blood glucose is 1.5 mmol/L. Learners treat shock and hypoglycaemia and move to rehydration (Plan C).
cases.learners: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children

cases.title: ETAT facilitator guide, Scenario 11: 18-month-old with fever, fast breathing and a convulsion
cases.learner: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: A boy with 2 days of fever and abdominal pain is grunting with subcostal recession, then starts to convulse; his glucose is low. Learners manage severe respiratory distress and learn that the seizure stops only when glucose is given.
cases.learners: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children

cases.title: ETAT facilitator guide, Scenario 12: 10-week-old who will not suckle
cases.learner: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: A 3.5 kg baby cried a lot yesterday and will not suckle today; he is hot, irritable and jittery with a blood glucose of 1 mmol/L. Learners triage as priority, give glucose and reach the diagnosis of meningitis with hypoglycaemia.
cases.learners: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children

cases.title: ETAT facilitator guide, Scenario 13: 1-year-old with severe dehydration
cases.learner: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: A listless 10 kg girl with 2 days of diarrhoea and vomiting will not drink, has sunken eyes and a very slow skin pinch. Learners classify severe dehydration, check for severe malnutrition and give Plan C IV (intravenous) fluids.
cases.learners: Doctors, nurses and clinical officers who see sick children

cases.title: IMCI distance learning, Module 2 opening case: Mimi, 6-week-old who stopped feeding
cases.learner: First-level health workers (nurses, clinical officers, community health staff)
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: Young mother Biya brings her first baby, Mimi, who has stopped attaching to the breast; Mimi is cold (34.7 C) and has lost weight since birth. Learners assess a young infant for very severe disease, classify and arrange urgent referral while communicating with a worried caregiver.
cases.learners: First-level health workers (nurses, clinical officers, community health staff)

cases.title: IMCI distance learning, Module 2 exercise: Sashi, 1-week-old with a rash
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: A caregiver brings a 1-week-old girl with a red rash and a few skin pustules on the buttocks; she feeds well and has no danger signs. Learners check for severe disease and local bacterial infection and classify the infant.

cases.title: IMCI distance learning, Module 3 opening case: Jacob, 6 months, cough and fast breathing
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: Amira walked 2 hours carrying 6-month-old Jacob, who is feeding poorly and breathing fast; she fears her husband will be angry. Learners check danger signs, count breathing, classify pneumonia and counsel the mother on oral antibiotics.

cases.title: IMCI distance learning, Module 4 opening case: Mary with several days of diarrhoea
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: Working mother Ana brings her daughter Mary, whose diarrhoea has lasted several days despite extra porridge; Ana feels guilty for waiting. Learners assess dehydration, classify the diarrhoea and teach home fluids and feeding.

cases.title: IMCI distance learning, Module 5 opening case: Sami, feeling hot in a malaria area
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: Miriam brings her quiet son Sami, who has felt hot for 2 days; the family lives in a high malaria risk area. Learners decide if the child has fever, assess malaria risk and test, and classify the fever.

cases.title: IMCI distance learning, Module 6 opening case: Noah with pale palms and a low MUAC
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: Tired mother Rachel travels by bus with Noah, who has very pale palms; his weight, height and mid-upper arm circumference must be checked. Learners assess for acute malnutrition and anaemia, classify and give feeding advice.

cases.title: IMCI distance learning, Module 8 opening case: Peter, 6 months, cough, mother recently diagnosed with HIV
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: Lungile brings 6-month-old Peter, who has coughed for 3 days and breathes 54 times a minute; she was recently told she has HIV (human immunodeficiency virus). Learners classify the cough and the child's HIV status and counsel the mother sensitively on testing and care.

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Depression module, Role play 1: assessment
cases.learner: Non-specialist health workers (nurses, doctors, clinical officers)
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A person has felt sad, exhausted, unable to sleep or concentrate, and has lost appetite and interest for two months, and fears losing their job. The provider assesses for depression with the mhGAP-IG; optional twists add a past manic episode or thyroid symptoms.
cases.learners: Non-specialist health workers (nurses, doctors, clinical officers)

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Depression module, Role play 2: psychosocial interventions
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 27-year-old who worked at a busy bank became depressed a year ago after his fiancee left him and work stress grew before a promotion; he was then fired and is now isolated with money problems. The provider delivers psychoeducation and a plan of psychosocial interventions such as stress reduction and social support.

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Depression module, Role play 3: Sarah and antidepressant choice
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Sarah has moderate-severe depression and is nervous about starting medicine. The provider explains drug options, benefits and side effects; an extended version adds a past manic episode that changes the plan.

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Depression module, Role play 4: Javier, 17, bullied at school
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Javier has felt sad for three months, sleeps and eats poorly and has stopped playing football because a bully harasses and hits him. The provider gives psychoeducation and addresses psychosocial stressors with an adolescent.

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Psychoses module, Role play 1: Mr Fadel, homeless man hearing a voice
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Mr Fadel, who sleeps in the park and drinks heavily, asks for food and money, struggles to answer, and keeps telling a threatening voice to be quiet. The provider assesses for psychosis with patience and simple language.

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Epilepsy module, Role play 3: Nikolaj, 17, seizures and school exclusion
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Nikolaj has episodes of a strange smell, blackout, shaking and incontinence, and was sent home from school two years ago out of stigma. The provider does emergency assessment and management; role plays 4 and 5 continue his diagnosis and six-month follow-up.

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Substance use module, Role play 1: alcohol dependence found at a hypertension visit
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: On a second visit for newly found high blood pressure, a person who lost a factory job drinks 10 to 12 drinks a day, shakes after six hours without alcohol, but downplays it. The provider uses the mhGAP-IG to assess harmful use and dependence.

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Substance use module, Role play 3: Mr Sana and motivational interviewing
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Mr Sana calls himself a social drinker but binges 7 to 9 drinks at weekend parties, has blackouts, wakes with cuts and hears he fights with his wife. The provider practises motivational interviewing; role play 4 continues with a plan to cut down.

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Substance use module, Emergency role play 1: Koya, opioid overdose
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Koya, a 28-year-old mother of three who injects heroin, relapsed after a costly detox and used a larger dose; she is slumped, very drowsy and breathing slowly. The provider follows the mhGAP (WHO Mental Health Gap Action Programme) emergency algorithm for a sedated person.

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Self-harm/suicide module, Role play 1: assessment after a motorcycle fall
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A young person hit the curb on a motorcycle while upset about exam results, has not slept or eaten, and thinks about driving off a bridge. The provider gently uncovers suicidal thoughts and plans, and identifies family support as protection.

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Self-harm/suicide module, Role play 2: pesticide ingestion after childbirth
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 30-year-old woman is stable on the ward after drinking pesticide; her baby is under a month old, she cannot sleep and has no desire to hold the baby. The provider practises psychosocial management; role play 3 is her follow-up visit.

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Self-harm/suicide module, Role play 4: Anika, 18, cut her arms after a family argument
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Anika came with her father after cutting her arms during a fight about a friendship her parents oppose; she does not want to die and does not want to stay in hospital. The provider assesses risk and manages self-harm with the family present.

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Other significant complaints module, Role play 1: woman beaten by her husband
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 35-year-old mother of three is beaten on the body by her husband, who drinks and uses drugs, takes her wages and also beats the children. The provider practises assessment and management after exposure to extreme stress and violence.

cases.title: mhGAP ToHP, Dementia module, Role play 1: Ingrid, 73, brought by her daughter
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Farah brings her 73-year-old mother Ingrid, who has become forgetful and vague since her husband died and sometimes does not recognize old friends. The provider assesses for dementia and the carer's needs; role play 2 covers wandering and a fall at follow-up.

cases.title: WHO dengue handbook, Section 4, Case study one: adult with missed shock and hidden bleeding
cases.learner: Doctors and nurses in emergency and inpatient care
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: A previously well 32-year-old man with 5 days of fever, vomiting and diarrhoea arrives drowsy with a pulse of 165 and a narrow pulse pressure. The timeline shows how shock and severe bleeding were missed and why fresh whole blood was needed.
cases.learners: Doctors and nurses in emergency and inpatient care

cases.title: WHO dengue handbook, Section 4, Case study two: 7-year-old girl with persistently high haematocrit
cases.learner: Doctors and nurses in emergency and inpatient care
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: A 7-year-old girl referred with high fever, cough and runny nose goes through the critical phase of dengue. The case teaches when to reduce IV (intravenous) fluids in a well-perfused child to avoid fluid overload.
cases.learners: Doctors and nurses in emergency and inpatient care

cases.title: WHO dengue handbook, Section 4, Case study three: 10-month-old with fever and seizures
cases.learner: Doctors and nurses in emergency and inpatient care
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: A previously well 10-month-old girl with 5 days of fever, poor intake, a passing rash, vomiting and diarrhoea arrives after 30 minutes of generalized seizures. Learners interpret staged lab results and manage severe dengue in an infant.
cases.learners: Doctors and nurses in emergency and inpatient care

cases.title: WHO dengue handbook, Section 4, Case study four: young woman misdiagnosed as hepatitis or gallbladder disease
cases.learner: Doctors and nurses in emergency and inpatient care
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: A 24-year-old woman with 3 days of fever, dark urine and mild jaundice is triaged as not urgent and labelled hepatitis, then gallbladder disease. The case shows how unexplained low platelets and a high haematocrit should point to dengue.
cases.learners: Doctors and nurses in emergency and inpatient care

cases.title: SAM course Module 3, Case 2: Ram, 9 months, severe wasting with diarrhoea
cases.learner: Doctors and nurses on paediatric wards
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Ram, 4.4 kg at 64 cm, has fed poorly for 3 weeks and has had loose stools and vomiting for 3 days with some dehydration and mild skin changes. Learners fill in the Critical Care Pathway and plan careful rehydration and feeding for a severely wasted child.
cases.learners: Doctors and nurses on paediatric wards

cases.title: SAM course Module 3, Case 3: Irena, 25 months, severe wasting and shock
cases.learner: Doctors and nurses on paediatric wards
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Irena has had diarrhoea and vomiting for 10 days, weighs 6.1 kg, is semi-conscious with cold hands, slow capillary refill, a fast pulse and pus from one eye. Learners manage shock in a severely malnourished child as a group exercise.
cases.learners: Doctors and nurses on paediatric wards

cases.title: SAM course Module 3 exercise, Case 3: John, 15 months, lethargic and cold
cases.learner: Doctors and nurses on paediatric wards
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: John has been unwell for 5 weeks, has had no food for 3 days and arrives limp; his temperature does not register on a standard thermometer. Learners decide on immediate treatment for hypothermia and low blood sugar.
cases.learners: Doctors and nurses on paediatric wards

cases.title: WHO ENC 1 simulation card, Case 4: The Golden Minute, ventilate
cases.learner: Midwives, nurses and doctors who attend births
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A baby is born and is not crying or breathing well after drying and stimulation. Learners start bag-and-mask ventilation within the Golden Minute while the mother or helper gives prompts, then debrief.
cases.learners: Midwives, nurses and doctors who attend births

cases.title: WHO ENC 1 simulation card, Case 5: no chest movement during ventilation
cases.learner: Midwives, nurses and doctors who attend births
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A baby is not breathing and the chest does not move with ventilation. Learners correct head position, mask seal and airway to improve ventilation and communicate with the mother.
cases.learners: Midwives, nurses and doctors who attend births

cases.title: WHO ENC 1 simulation card, Case 6: decide on advanced care
cases.learner: Midwives, nurses and doctors who attend births
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A baby is still not breathing but the chest moves with bag-and-mask ventilation. Learners check heart rate, continue ventilation and decide on advanced care and referral.
cases.learners: Midwives, nurses and doctors who attend births

cases.title: WHO ENC 2 simulation card, Case 3: 1900 g baby who cannot attach
cases.learner: Midwives, nurses and doctors caring for newborns
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: At 90 minutes of age a 1900 g baby with a normal temperature can swallow but cannot attach to the breast. Learners provide intermediate care for a small baby and explain the plan to the mother.
cases.learners: Midwives, nurses and doctors caring for newborns

cases.title: WHO ENC 2 simulation card, Case 5: 1900 g baby with fast breathing and grunting
cases.learner: Midwives, nurses and doctors caring for newborns
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 1900 g baby breathes fast from birth and by 4 hours has chest indrawing, grunting, 100 breaths a minute and has not fed. Learners recognize a small baby who needs advanced care and act on it; the card set includes an antibiotic dosing table.
cases.learners: Midwives, nurses and doctors caring for newborns

cases.title: HBB 2nd edition OSCE A: term baby with meconium who needs ventilation
cases.license: Copyright American Academy of Pediatrics, all rights reserved; free download for training use
cases.brief: The learner prepares for a term birth; the baby is born through meconium-stained fluid, does not cry and has meconium blocking the mouth. The examiner reads prompts and scores drying, airway clearing and effective bag-and-mask ventilation.

cases.title: HBB 2nd edition OSCE B: 34-week baby who does not breathe
cases.license: Copyright American Academy of Pediatrics, all rights reserved; free download for training use
cases.brief: The learner attends the birth of a 34-week baby with clear fluid who is not crying. The checklist scores the Golden Minute steps, ventilation and reassessment.

cases.title: ECEB OSCE B: 1700 g baby at 1 hour who could not breastfeed
cases.learner: Nurses, midwives and doctors caring for newborns
cases.license: Copyright American Academy of Pediatrics, all rights reserved; free download for training use
cases.brief: A 1700 g baby is 60 minutes old; eye care, cord care and vitamin K are done, and she stayed skin-to-skin but could not breastfeed. The learner shows how to assess and care for a small baby within the OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination: a timed exam station where a student sees a standardized patient) time limit.
cases.learners: Nurses, midwives and doctors caring for newborns

cases.title: HMS Pre-eclampsia and Eclampsia flip chart: opening role play, day-1 postpartum woman with severe headache who convulses
cases.learner: Midwives, nurses and doctors who manage births
cases.license: Copyright Jhpiego, all rights reserved; free download from Jhpiego
cases.brief: A woman one day after birth complains of a severe headache, then convulses and loses consciousness in front of the group. The unannounced role play opens the course and shows why every provider must be ready to act on eclampsia.
cases.learners: Midwives, nurses and doctors who manage births

cases.title: HMS Pre-eclampsia and Eclampsia flip chart: Mrs C, 27, 39 weeks, in labour with very high blood pressure
cases.learner: Midwives, nurses and doctors who manage births
cases.license: Copyright Jhpiego, all rights reserved; free download from Jhpiego
cases.brief: Mrs C, pregnant with her first baby, is in labour at 4 cm with normal antenatal visits; if assessed, her blood pressure is 178/112 with 2+ urine protein (case 2 adds blurred vision). The facilitator plays Mrs C while up to three learners diagnose severe pre-eclampsia and start treatment, then debrief on teamwork and respectful care.
cases.learners: Midwives, nurses and doctors who manage births

cases.title: HMS Pre-eclampsia and Eclampsia flip chart: Mrs K, arrives by ambulance after an eclamptic fit
cases.learner: Midwives, nurses and doctors at referral facilities
cases.license: Copyright Jhpiego, all rights reserved; free download from Jhpiego
cases.brief: Mrs K, 38 weeks, arrives with a referral card saying she had an eclamptic fit and received a magnesium sulfate loading dose three hours ago; she has no urinary catheter. Learners rapidly reassess and continue treatment, including blood pressure control and a strict fluid balance chart.
cases.learners: Midwives, nurses and doctors at referral facilities

cases.title: WHO Bleeding after birth course, Scenario practice 1: PPH prevention
cases.learner: All health workers who care for women at birth
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A woman gives birth on the simulator. Learners check for a second baby, give a uterotonic within one minute, deliver the placenta with controlled cord traction, check tone, placenta and tears, and record blood loss and shock index.
cases.learners: All health workers who care for women at birth

cases.title: WHO Bleeding after birth course, Scenario practice 2: 500 mL loss with a soft uterus
cases.learner: All health workers who care for women at birth
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Right after birth the uterus is soft and the measurement tool shows 500 mL. Learners diagnose PPH (postpartum hemorrhage), call for help with SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation: a handover format), assign team roles and start the PPH bundle.
cases.learners: All health workers who care for women at birth

cases.title: WHO Bleeding after birth course, Scenario practice 3: under 500 mL but abnormal vital signs
cases.learner: All health workers who care for women at birth
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Fifteen minutes after birth the uterus is soft and loss is under 500 mL, but pulse is 110 and blood pressure 90/64. Learners calculate the shock index, recognize PPH (postpartum hemorrhage) from warning signs and act.
cases.learners: All health workers who care for women at birth

cases.title: WHO Bleeding after birth course, Scenario practice 4: retained placenta with heavy bleeding
cases.learner: All health workers who care for women at birth
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: The placenta will not deliver, the uterus is soft and blood flow is heavy. Learners call for help, communicate with SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation: a handover format) and manage a retained placenta within the PPH (postpartum hemorrhage) bundle.
cases.learners: All health workers who care for women at birth

cases.title: WHO Bleeding after birth course, Scenario practice 5: still bleeding after the PPH bundle
cases.learner: All health workers who care for women at birth
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: After the bundle the woman keeps bleeding with pulse 112 and blood pressure 94/60. Learners call for more help and escalate care using the course steps for bleeding that continues after the bundle.
cases.learners: All health workers who care for women at birth

cases.title: PEN training modules, type 2 diabetes session, Case study 2: older woman with low consciousness
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 68-year-old woman with diabetes for 3 years comes in drowsy with a random blood sugar of 50 mg/dL. Learners recognize severe hypoglycaemia and treat with sugar by mouth or IV (intravenous) glucose, then reassess.

cases.title: PEN training modules, hypertension session, Case 1: smoker with one raised blood pressure reading
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 45-year-old man who smokes has a first-ever blood pressure of 145/80 at a screening visit. Learners confirm the reading correctly before labelling hypertension, assess other risks and address smoking.

cases.title: PEN training modules, stroke session, Scenario 1: weakness and speech difficulty for two hours
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 60-year-old male smoker has had left-sided weakness starting with numbness two hours ago and now some difficulty talking. Learners use the suspected acute stroke algorithm to build a management plan; the session also has a FAST community role play.

cases.title: PEN training modules, stroke session, Scenario 2: diabetic woman with a passing episode of weakness
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 50-year-old woman with diabetes comes for a sugar check and mentions sudden left arm weakness and slurred speech three days ago that fully recovered. Learners apply the suspected acute stroke algorithm to symptoms that have fully resolved.

cases.title: PEN training modules, COPD and asthma session, Case study 4: smoker with years of cough and breathlessness
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: A 55-year-old man has smoked 12 hand-rolled cigarettes a day for 23 years and has 4 years of worsening breathlessness and winter productive cough. Learners explain why this is COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) rather than asthma and which tests to do; case 5 adds a non-smoking woman exposed to cooking smoke.

cases.title: PEN training modules, oral cancer session, Case 1: Mr Raj, betel nut user who cannot open his mouth well
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Mr Raj, 35, has chewed betel nut for 5 years and has pain opening his mouth, stained teeth, white patches and leathery mucosa. Learners suspect oral submucous fibrosis, advise quitting with the 5A's and refer.

cases.title: PEN training modules, oral cancer session, Case 2: Ms Rani with a non-healing ulcer
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Ms Rani, 45, has a mouth ulcer that has not healed for 2 weeks, with a red velvety patch and some white patches. Learners recognize probable erythroplakia and refer for biopsy.

cases.title: PEN training modules, RHD prevention session, Role plays 1 to 4: sore throat, rheumatic fever, RHD and secondary prophylaxis
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Two participants play a health worker and a patient in four linked role plays: a sore throat, suspected rheumatic fever, suspected heart damage needing referral, and a known RHD (rheumatic heart disease) patient missing penicillin injections. Learners practise explaining the strep throat to RHD pathway and counselling for adherence.

cases.title: PEN training modules, harmful alcohol use session: Mahesh Babu brief intervention role play
cases.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
cases.brief: Mahesh Babu, a 35-year-old government worker and father of three, drinks after work, comes home drunk, has relapsed many times and now drinks from daybreak. One volunteer plays him while another delivers a 5A's and 5R's brief intervention and observers give feedback.

cases.title: IMAI TB-HIV participant's manual, chapter 3 case study: John, 25, four weeks of cough
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: John, a healthy married father of two, has coughed for four weeks, now brings up yellow mucus and has fevers worse at night. Learners decide how to manage and counsel a person with suspected TB (tuberculosis); the case returns in later chapters.

cases.title: IMAI TB-HIV participant's manual, chapter 4 case study: Mugisha, very ill and thin
cases.license: Copyright WHO, all rights reserved (free to read and download; ask WHO for reuse permission)
cases.brief: Just before closing, a family carries in Mugisha, 34, very thin, coughing for 2 months with chest pain and night sweats; his HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) status is unknown. Learners decide how to assess and manage a very sick person with possible TB (tuberculosis) and unknown HIV status.

cases.title: RHDAustralia e-learning: Michael's Story
cases.learner: First Nations health workers and practitioners, primary care clinicians
cases.license: Free with registration; RHDAustralia and Heart Foundation terms
cases.brief: An animated story follows Michael, a 14-year-old Aboriginal boy, and his Aunty Mary when he sees the doctor with a sore knee and fever and acute rheumatic fever is suspected. Learners follow his journey through diagnosis and penicillin treatment and the health worker's support role.
cases.learners: First Nations health workers and practitioners, primary care clinicians

about_html:
About this library

What the Global Casebook is

The Global Casebook helps a teacher find a free practice patient for a condition their students will meet. Each case comes from a trusted publisher. Most have been peer reviewed. Many include the materials an actor needs to play the patient: the patient's story, what to say, the physical findings, and a checklist to mark the student.

How to use it

  • By condition. Type a disease, an abbreviation or a symptom in the search field. The list suggests matching conditions as you type. Select one to see every case for it.
  • By country. Select a partner country. You see the conditions with the highest burden there, from the WHO (World Health Organization) estimates. Open a condition to see its cases.
  • Coverage and gaps. The table shows which priority conditions have many cases, few cases, or none.
  • Labels on each case. "SP materials included" means the publication gives a script or case for a standardized patient. "Adaptable for an SP" means a simulation or paper case that a teacher can turn into an SP encounter.

How we built it

  1. Partner countries. We took the ten international partner countries from the Global Health Academy website in September 2026, and added the United States for the domestic partners (Sacred Heart, UConn, Yale, WestConn and Puerto Rico).
  2. Top conditions. For each country we took the leading causes of disease burden from one source, the WHO Global Health Estimates, so that countries can be compared. COVID-19 is left out because pandemic years distort the ranks. Where a condition is a known national priority but falls below the top ten (for example malaria, tuberculosis, HIV (human immunodeficiency virus), dengue or sickle cell disease), we added it as a local priority, marked "LOCAL", with its own WHO or national source.
  3. MedEdPORTAL. We read the title and abstract of every MedEdPORTAL publication, 3,346 in total from 2005 to September 2026, using the open OpenAlex index. We kept each publication that contains a patient case usable for a standardized patient, OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination: a timed exam station where a student sees a standardized patient), role-play or simulation. Procedure-only trainers, lectures, curricula and surveys were left out.
  4. Cross-reference. Each case is tagged with the conditions it teaches. A condition with five or more cases is marked well covered, one to four is thin, and none is a gap.
  5. Other trusted sources. For the gaps, we searched for free cases from WHO training courses, peer-reviewed simulation journals, open-access case report journals, national programs and university repositories.
  6. Verification. Every MedEdPORTAL title was matched to the publisher's DOI (Digital Object Identifier: a permanent link to a publication) record and every DOI link was opened. Every WHO burden figure was compared with the live WHO data. Each other figure was checked against its source document, and eight were corrected. Every other case link was opened, and each case was checked in PubMed Central, WHO IRIS or on its own page. The Sources tab shows the results.

Limits

  • The case summaries and condition tags come from the published abstracts, read with the help of AI and checked by sampling. Open the case and read it before you use it with students.
  • Most MedEdPORTAL cases were written for training in the United States. Drugs, tests and referral paths may differ from your setting. Adapt them to local guidelines.
  • Each case keeps its own license. MedEdPORTAL cases are free to use for teaching; most are CC BY-NC-SA or CC BY. Credit the authors when you use or adapt a case.
  • Burden ranks describe deaths and years of healthy life lost for the whole population. They do not describe what a single clinic sees each day.

Run a case with a virtual patient

The eight patients in the free Virtual Standardized Patient tool come from six MedEdPORTAL publications in this library. They run offline in that tool, where a local AI model plays the patient on a laptop with no internet connection.
